name: Repentance & assurance
about: Godly sorrow, confession, and the believer kept by God.

teachings.title: Thou art my hiding place
teachings.summary: Those who have called on the Lord can rest assured they are saved and preserved, already forgiven, and should come willingly to walk in His ways.
teachings.text:
Those who have heard and responded to the truth, who in the appointed day prayed unto Him, can rest assured that we are saved.

*Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah.*

This is the hope we have. The same hope the congregations of the children of Israel sang of in the temple of Solomon, with the songs of his father echoing this blessed promise, centuries before the first coming of Christ Jesus.

And God responds to His children, in this inspired Psalm. Promising to teach and guide us in His ways. He asks we come willingly. That we have understanding to walk with Him in His ways, and not be like the horse or mule, needing a bit and bridle to pull us along. His yoke is light. The burden is easy.

The wicked may suffer their sorrows of their own making, but we who are forgiven by His mercy because we trust in the Lord, are preserved. What an amazing relief to know we are already forgiven. That we may come boldly before God to sing His praises, glorifying Him for His mercies' sake.

*Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, ye righteous: and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart.* Amen!

teachings.title: I shall be satisfied when I awake with thy likeness
teachings.summary: God keeps His children under His wing, and our satisfaction is in the resurrection when we shall see Christ and be like Him, whatever the wicked gain now.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalms 17**, we see that David's importunity comes from his faith in God to hear those who call upon Him. That we may go boldly before the throne of grace, because He has shown us that He listens to our cries. The initial call for salvation in the Lord's name gives us the hope that He listens to us for far less important matters, such as our suffering in this life.

The Lord's lovingkindness is already apparent to those that put their trust in Him, that have been saved by His strong right-hand. Christ Jesus. We know that our Savior is at the right hand of the Father. The New Testament is clear on this. But David is writing hundreds of years earlier, showing that Old Testament saints knew and understood the concept, even if they didn't have the full revelation and details.

*Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings, From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.*

Keep me, o Lord. It is His power that keeps the children of God under His protection and secure in His promises. We shall not fear, because we are under His mighty wing, as a mother hen keeps her chicks.

Jesus laments the unfaithful Jews for refusing to be gathered thus.

**Matthew 23:37–39**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord*.

And His protection is needed in this world, where they hate us for His holy name. Where we are often at the mercy of forces beyond our reckoning. Where the judgment of God against our nation is executed by the hands of the wicked. They are His sword.

They may profit in this life. They may have riches, while we are poor. They may have children and an inheritance. But we have the eternal promise of Christ, which is far more precious than any treasure of this life.

*As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.*

This is the eternal perspective that Christians should seek. That our satisfaction is in the resurrection, and the current, temporal troubles are nothing compared to the everlasting.

When we awake, when we are raised up, we will see Jesus, the express likeness of God. But, maybe David is also speaking of the glorified body we will receive in His likeness.

**1 John 3:1–2**
*Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.*

This is our blessed hope. To awake into glory with Him. When we see Jesus as sons of God. Gathered up to the Lord, and with Him shall we ever be.

Ultimately, this is the only satisfaction we need. If our enemies prosper, if God allows them to have advantage over us, while we suffer them, we know His grace is sufficient. That ultimately, vengeance will be His. That in the Lord's love for us, we will see Him as He is, and be like Him.

That no matter what may come in this life, we have peace in the next. Amen

teachings.title: Once you drink the water of life
teachings.summary: One who has truly believed the gospel will never utterly turn from it, because the indwelling Spirit leaves no room for the spirit of error and the elect cannot be deceived.
teachings.text:
Once you are saved, when you hear the truth and believe it unto salvation, you will never reject it utterly. You will never turn fully away from it, to seek another way of salvation.

Once you have partaken and drank the water of life, you will never thirst again. How could you? The Spirit is now within you, satisfying that thirst for truth. The bread, His words of eternal life are eaten, and you will never hunger again.

It's hard not to see this truth everywhere in the Bible when you look for it. The promise of God that all who believe shall not be condemned. That all who drink freely of those living waters will never thirst again, let alone for something less than the truth of God's promise. The Spirit of truth does not leave room for the spirit of error. For the spirit of antichrist. For the spirit of Babylon. It is not possible to deceive the very elect.

teachings.title: He that endureth to the end shall be saved
teachings.summary: Enduring to the end is about being saved out of tribulation and persecution, not about keeping eternal life, which cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
Amos continues, calling upon that remnant of Joseph, those who seek the Lord, to hate the evil and love the good, that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious to them in this tribulation.

We need to keep this in mind, ourselves. Things are going to be bad, waxing worse and worse. The patience of the saints, our "enduring to the end," is found in this instruction to hate evil, love good and establish judgement and righteousness.

Too many false teachers assert that perseverance is for our spiritual salvation, that we could lose the free gift of eternal life, but that is not the context or meaning of it. It is for grace and protection during tribulation and persecution.

**Matthew 24:9-13**
*Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.*

Saved from the persecution. Saved out of great tribulation.

**Revelation 7:14**
*And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.*

teachings.title: The truth dwelleth in us for ever
teachings.summary: A believer can never lose salvation or fall into apostasy, because the truth dwells in him forever; one who departs to another belief never had the truth.
teachings.text:
**2 John 1-3**
*The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth; For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever. Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.*

Once again, if a person has believed in their heart that Jesus Christ died for their sins, and received the baptism of the holy Spirit, made a child of God, they can NEVER lose their salvation.

And further, THEY CAN NEVER fall into apostasy. They may backslide, become castaway and chastised by God, not produce works or fruits and even forget their own salvation, but they will NEVER believe anything other than the truth of the gospel, because the truth dwells within us and shall be with us forever.

If a person who claims to be a Christian departs from the faith to believe something else as true, a false gospel or atheism or any other deception, the truth was never in them.

teachings.title: The two Sauls of Benjamin
teachings.summary: King Saul was saved but backslid by pleasing men until God gave him an ignoble death, while Saul of Tarsus of the same tribe kept under his flesh lest he be a castaway.
teachings.text:
And so we come to the end of Saul, a Benjamite, son of Cis, or Kish as it is in the Old Testament. A man head and shoulders above the other men of Israel. Anointed by God to be their first king.

And while Saul was most assuredly saved, his life as king was not the example of a Christian walk that we aspire too.

We see him developing from a loyal son, seeking the lost donkey of his father, to an unsteady and uncertain leader, plucked from the least tribe of Israel, just a generation removed from their decimation for harboring sodomites. Every bit the part of king, but with none of the heart to lead.

Saul spends his time as King worrying about what others think of him, what they may do or say. Caring about the world over the word of God. Indecisive. Prone to bad choices. And ultimately paranoid and wrathful, knowing the Lord had repented of his kingship and had chosen another to take his place. David, the apple of God's eye. A man after the Lord's own heart.

Now to Saul and his sons would have been the promises given to David. But his transgressions against the Lord were too great. And even with warning after warning, Saul back slid further and further.

Had this Saul repented, and confessed his sin and asked for forgiveness, he may have been restored. But he was blinded by the evil spirit given him by God for his disobedience. Seeking the witch of Endor was the final straw, and God gave him an ignoble death, and a fitting end, along with his sons.

It is fitting that of all the people God could choose to use to spread the gospel to the Gentiles, He found a man of Benjamin named Saul, also known as Paul (his Roman name), the name and the tribe redeemed by Paul's dedication to the word of God.

We see that, following his conversion on the road to Damascus, where he was blinded by God but restored by His word, when he sought out Ananias and was healed, Saul/Paul did his best to keep the word of God, and to not be castaway. Mortifying his flesh against sin. Preaching hard against backsliding and for separation from the world. A man who risked being rejected by his own people, being tortured, stoned, persecuted, arrested, held in bonds for years, and likely died for the cause of Christ.

The two Saul's of Benjamin couldn't have been more different. But both were the anointed of God.

teachings.title: God gives many chances, but chastens compromise
teachings.summary: Saul never lost his salvation but became a castaway, showing obedience is not for salvation but saved people are held to a higher standard and chastened for compromise and the sins they find appealing.
teachings.text:
This chapter contains some key scripture and doctrines, but the primary message for Christians here is the understanding God will give us multiple chances to be used by Him for His purpose, if we harken to His word. Follow His commandments. And every time we turn rather to what seems right in our own eyes, or add too or diminish His word, or compromise to please men, He is grieved.

Saul, His anointed remains king until his death. But the Lord is no longer with him. The word of the Lord taken away with Samuel. Saul was castaway. He never stopped believing, never lost his salvation, but he no longer would receive the blessings and benefits, and he would backslide into vanity and wickedness. Pride and paranoia, until he lost everything including his own life.

People who doubt the gospel will often slanderously report that we teach a license to sin. But in truth, we who are saved are held to a higher standard. To whom much is given, much is expected. The chastisement of God is fierce against our sin.

Obedience to the Lord is not for our spiritual salvation, but rather that it be well with us and we may be His workmen doing great things for the Lord. When we compromise with the world, seek approval from men, we are dealt with more harshly.

When God sent Saul to slay the Amalek, he and the people had no problem with the genocide to be carried out when it was against things that were vile and refuse. But when they saw nice things, *the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good,* they stayed their hand and thought better of themselves than what God commands.

Christians do this too. It is easy to eliminate many sins in our lives. To stop doing vile things, while in the Spirit. But the sin that is appealing, that seems good and profitable in our eyes. That we struggle with eliminating.

And sometimes, like Saul, we even convince ourselves God can use it to His glory. That by not eliminating it from our lives we are actually doing right. Rationalizing evil by calling it good.

But God will not be impressed with our rebellion.

teachings.title: Saul was saved, yet his end was tragic
teachings.summary: Saul was truly saved by grace through faith, but a believer who forgets God's word and will not confess when chastened can lose his blessings and even be called home early.
teachings.text:
It really can be difficult to recognize that Saul was saved. He believed on the Lord. It becomes harder and harder to keep that perspective going forward, as we read through **Samuel**. But Saul was certainly saved by grace through faith in the Lord.

His victories, the times the Lord used him for good for His people, where he was blessed personally, all show that even a less than perfect Christian can still have a great impact. But there are pitfalls and snares that we all face. And our end can be as tragic as Saul's if we allow ourselves to forget the word of God and to stay on the path He leads us. If we lean on our own understanding. If we don't recognize our error when chastised, and ask for forgiveness. The longsuffering of God has limits and He will take from us blessings and eventually even call us home if we no longer can be useful to His works that He has crafted us to do.

teachings.title: The evil report against eternal security
teachings.summary: Like the ten spies, those who deny eternal security spread fear and doubt, while Caleb's faith pictures trusting Christ's promise that none can pluck us from His hand.
teachings.text:
There are lessons in these stories that are for our benefit as Christians. Here we see how doubt can lead to disputations, and even when assurances of the bold in faith come, many people cling to fear and would rather believe a bad report than trust in the Lord and His word. For this cause, many who seek salvation turn away.

Probably the biggest stumbling block people get caught on is the idea of eternal security. That once we are saved, we are always saved. That our faith in Christ is unto redemption. Not only that He exists. Not only that He is the Son of God. Not only that He lived, died for us and was raised again from the dead, but that the earnest of our redemption is given us, the Spirit that indwells and quickens us, sealing us, and that in no way shall we be cast out. That we may know we have eternal life.

*And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one.*

This is the promise made by Jesus. That we are given the Kingdom of Heaven by faith in Him. The promised land.

Speaking in the spirit of Caleb, Paul boldly testifies;

*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

Yet, those seeking the truth may need our testimony. They may need us to spy out the land and confirm to them from scripture exactly what God said that they may believe. To boldly proclaim His Gospel.

But there will be many, including those who claim to be of God, who give a bad report. Who tell people that their problems are insurmountable. That their sins are like giants and they are as grasshoppers. That to enter the promised land would be death.

And so fear and doubt spread and keep people from accepting the truth. From trusting in the Lord to deliver them.

This is the spirit of fear and doubt that uses the lie that eternal security doesn't exist. That you can lose your salvation. That because you are small and weak, you won't make it. You won't "persevere to the end." That you must "Repent-of-your-sins!" That if you fail to produce "fruit" by the judgment of men that you cannot make it to Heaven.

But we see here, God was providing the fruit, in a size and abundance that they could not even imagine. Joshua and Caleb showed them the fruit that comes from trusting in the Lord.

And yet they saw their fears as bigger than their God.

teachings.title: Nothing can separate us from the love of God
teachings.summary: Once the Spirit seals the believer nothing can separate him from God, so once saved always saved is the truth of the gospel itself.
teachings.text:
*What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us? He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth. Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.*

*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

Another side note, from another clear and concise conclusion to another argument, made by Paul: We who believe are adopted into the faith that is without repentance. Eternal life of the gift. The Spirit creates a new man in the believers and seals us to the day of redemption, where we look forward to being raised up in glorified bodies. Our hope that we do not see but know is to come, the same Spirit testifying within us as the surety of the promise.

And nothing can separate us from God once we have received the Spirit, which is by faith, through grace.

We may know we have eternal life and that life is in Jesus.

Once saved always saved is not just a slogan, it is the truth of the Gospel and the crux of the Gospel, without which you cannot claim to have faith. You cannot claim to believe on Christ and at the same time maintain that it can be lost.

teachings.title: Our blessed hope of everlasting life
teachings.summary: Trusting the gospel includes trusting that faith gives everlasting life and the resurrection, and without that sure hope one does not truly believe.
teachings.text:
Really thinking about this and when when we talk about the Gospel, we of course talk about what one is trusting in to be saved. That God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believes on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.

Each part of that is true. Each part of it is important to believe. Without any aspect, you're missing the picture of what our faith is held in.

We not only believe that there is a God. That out of love for His creation, He sent His only begotten Son to die for us. That Jesus existed. That faith in His work not only saves us from Hell, but gives us eternal life.

It is that last bit that is our blessed hope. It is the unseen thing that we wait patiently for. That we are called to be longsuffering towards as we wait.

We seek the resurrection. To be shed of the sinful flesh and to fully be the new man. That is our hope. We await Jesus' return because that is the hour of our redemption. Where we are changed in a twinkling of an eye. Where corruption puts on incorruption.

If you aren't trusting God that that's a sure thing for believing Jesus died and rose again, when His word tells us again and again that that is the payoff for that faith, then you don't have a hope in Hell.

teachings.title: The good and evil figs
teachings.summary: The good figs carried captive and the rotten figs left show both God's mercy and wrath, and believers planted in Christ cannot be plucked up.
teachings.text:
Short chapter, but powerful. The Lord shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs. One very good, the other evil and inedible, and He tells the prophet that the very good figs are the remnant that was carried away in captivity to Nebuchadnezzar. He promised that the tribulation of this is to turn their heart towards God, and they will be returned to Jerusalem filled with zeal.

But the rotten figs represent the wicked of Judah, who will be scattered and bred out of existence, killed by the sword or by pestilence. To be a proverb and a byword for other nations, "see how they have fallen."

Both the saved remnant and the reprobates reveal the glory of God. In His mercy and deliverance from the worst of conditions, to a restored Jerusalem and His wrath against the ungodly who hold the truth in unrighteousness.

The same holds true today.

As **Romans 1:16-20** lays out;

 *For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.*

*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse*

This prophecy having dual fulfilment; that the Babylonian captivity will end, and some of Judah will be returned by the mercy and grace of God, and *they shall return unto Me with their whole heart*, and that the same will be true of those saved by faith in Christ after the resurrection.

*I will plant them, and not pluck them up. And I will give them an heart to know me, that I am the Lord: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God*.

**Hebrews 10:16-26**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

We are planted in Christ and cannot be plucked up. We are His people. A nation that was no nation. And He is our God.

teachings.title: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ
teachings.summary: No one can lay a charge against God's elect or take away their salvation, because the indwelling Spirit assures eternal security.
teachings.text:
*Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth.*

Who can say to us that are justified by the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, predestined in Him to be heirs of God, that our sin in the flesh has disqualified our spirit and the promise?

Who can tell you you've been taken from Him, if God's word is that we cannot lose what he has given us?

**John 10:28-30**
*And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one*.

The eternal security of salvation is the purpose of the Spirit indwelling us. That we may KNOW we have eternal life. That this wretched condition of the flesh will end. And the new man inside us will take on incorruption at the redemption.

Let no man tell you you can lose your salvation. Let no man lay change against you who are in Christ. Let no man lead you back to the yoke of the law, which is death. For we have eternal life with the Father through the Son, testified by the Spirit.

*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us. For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

Amen, amen, amen!

teachings.title: Hebrews 6 Does Not Teach Losing Salvation
teachings.summary: Hebrews 6 is twisted by the unlearned to teach that salvation can be lost, but God has sworn nothing can separate the believer from His love.
teachings.text:
Without controversy, the text of Hebrews, especially this chapter, is difficult. Complex "if-then" statements that rely on a foundational knowledge and understanding of scripture. Arguments that are braided with others, concepts that span multiple chapters and verses, and circle back upon themselves having detours to touch on other things. It is the meat of the word.

2 Peter 3:15-16
*And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.*

And as Peter writes, because of their difficult nature many twist the meaning, taking it out of context to arrive at false doctrines that contradict what's being taught. The unlearned and unstable.

And so many false prophets teach that Hebrews 6 is a warning that you can lose your salvation. As we see throughout scripture and from the handful of verses I posted at the beginning, God has sworn we cannot lose the free gift of eternal life that He has given us in His grace and mercy, purchased by the blood of Christ.

**Romans 8:38-39**
*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord*.

They cannot point to anything as clear as this to back their damnable heresy, and so they count on the ignorance and lack of understanding of those they seek to corrupt, and the complexity of **Hebrews 6**, to mislead.

What they never can do is explain their doctrine in light of the scriptures that directly contradict them. And so they leave it as a contradiction. Confusion. But *God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.*

And so, we can know with confidence that God's promise is true.

*He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

Amen

teachings.title: Blotted Out, Never Added to the Book of Life
teachings.summary: All are born into the book of life and are only blotted out through unbelief, reprobation or unpardonable sin; no one is ever added to it.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars;*

Again, Jesus is addressing a church, this in Sardis, and He uses descriptors of Himself from scripture to sign the message.

 *I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead.*
*Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.*

The church at Sardis has a reputation for being an active and lively congregation, but Jesus says He knows that's not the case. He warns them to return to what was preached unto them, that they won't die out completely. That His coming won't be a surprise to them, like a thief in the night overtaking them as He will the world of non-believers.

*Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy.*

His appeal then are to the genuinely saved among them in Sardis, encouraging them in their walk, and their reward in His return.

And then, again another message to the saved, who have overcome the world by their faith in Him:

*He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

The white raiment of the wedding feast, the garment we receive having been called by grace and accepting the invitation by faith. Whose names are not blotted out of the book of life.

Note, we are born into the book of life, we are blotted out by death as unbelievers, or reprobation, or unpardonable sin such as blasphemy of the Holy Ghost, knowingly adding to or taking away from the word of God or, as we will see, taking the mark of the beast. No one in the Bible is added to the book of life, only blotted out and removed having already been there. Understanding of this helps when faced with a few false doctrines.

Jesus promise to us who are saved is that He will confess our names before our Father, our counsel, the sole mediator we need.

teachings.title: His sons are always His sons
teachings.summary: Unlike Esau or the prodigal trying to work off debt, believers are adopted sons sealed and preserved by God, which is the theme of the whole Bible.
teachings.text:
People who, like Esau, seek to find forgiveness in their own works, or like the Prodigal Son, by thinking they are no longer welcome as a son, but have to work as a servant to repay what they did wrong, will often say "salvation by faith alone isn't in the Bible," or "Once saved, always saved" isn't. And yet, in dozens of clear verses, and in parable and story, we see how God rates forgiveness, how His sons are always His sons. That we are heirs to the kingdom through Christ, adopted to the promise. Not servants to work off debt. Not fumbling Esau, trying to emulate Jacob and regain favor.

The idea of forgiveness and adoption, being sealed by the Spirit, a son of God, by our faith, and maintained, preserved by God who is just and merciful, who forgets our sins when we confess them, who chastises us when we fail to recognize our error, who blesses us with abundance, in grace, unearned favor, is the entire theme of the Bible. The love of God for we who believe.

It's everything.

teachings.title: Vessels to honour and to dishonour
teachings.summary: In God's great house carnal believers are still saved but earthen vessels, which refutes Lordship salvation and perseverance, and we should sanctify ourselves to be gold and silver vessels.
teachings.text:
And being His, we are as vessels in His great house. Some earthen and wood. Carnal Christians. Who, while believing and part of the Kingdom, in the great house so to speak, but not being sanctified, are less suited to His purpose. He says not to be like they are, but to sanctify yourself that you become as the vessels made of gold and silver, meet for His use. For His good works.

This dispels the false doctrine and damnable heresy of Lordship/perseverance of the saints. We are all saved who believe. And some will sanctify themselves to honor, becoming more useful to God. Others won't be more than earthen pots, and dishonored.

But all are saved.

We should strive for gold and silver. For crowns. For mastery. To be a soldier for God. Enduring hardship for the sake of those who may believe and be saved.

teachings.title: Salvation cannot be lost, only refused
teachings.summary: The foolish virgins and unprofitable servant were never saved; they refused what was offered, for salvation cannot be lost, only refused.
teachings.text:
Some use these parables to teach that you can lose your salvation. That the foolish virgins and the unprofitable servant were saved, and having been sinful or disobedient, had lost their shot at Heaven. But there is nothing to this, for ALL are called. We all, every person, has been given the truth, written in our hearts, through creation, and have no excuse. God will that none perish. Every name is in the book of life until it's blotted out. When one dies, or is given over to reprobation or, in the end, refuses to repent and believe when the day of the Lord is come, it's too late. They are damned to eternal fire. To eternal torment.

The foolish virgins and unprofitable servant believed falsely, and what had been given them, the chance to enter into the joy of the Lord, is taken from them. Salvation cannot be lost, only refused.

Consider, had the five foolish virgins filled their lamps with oil at the first, they may still have slumbered and been lazy regarding their waiting for his return, but they still would have had that oil, the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, and still would have entered into the wedding with the five wise virgins.

Similarly, Jesus says that had the unprofitable servant simply thrown in the one talent of silver giving him, his own salvation, with others seeking to increase the harvest, he would have still entered into the joy of the Lord, the Kingdom of Heaven.

The Bible says in **Romans 4:5**
*But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.*

And while I would rather have great rewards in the kingdom, being given responsibility over much, or even responsibility over little, the goal is to be present at the bridegroom's wedding feast, to enter into the joy of the Lord.

Far too many reject the gift. Bury it in the ground and don't even use it for themselves, let alone accept it and bring increase to the Father, honoring the Son.

teachings.title: The unforgiving servant was never saved
teachings.summary: The unforgiving servant did not lose salvation but never truly received the king's free forgiveness, because in pride he never admitted he owed the debt.
teachings.text:
Another quick note on the story told by Jesus of the unforgiving servant, the ungracious servant. Note that when the king said he would forgive the incredible debt the servant had incurred, it was a blanket forgiveness offer, that had no other requirements of it except being humble enough to agree you owed it and being willing to throw yourself upon his mercy and accept it.

The unforgiving servant wasn't saved and then lost his salvation for being unforgiving. He was never saved because he never accepted that he truly owed that debt. He saw the king's offer in selfish terms and in pride, least he would have shown the same grace and mercy to the man who owed him little.

teachings.title: I am the resurrection and the life
teachings.summary: Jesus wept as one touched with our infirmities, and His word to Martha that whoever believes in Him shall never die is salvation by faith and eternal security.
teachings.text:
Jesus wept. The shortest verse in the Bible and perhaps one of the most powerful. Here his friend Lazarus has died, and his sisters are mourning and the emotion overwhelms Jesus even knowing He can and will raise Lazarus up. The pain of life and grief is something that Jesus being fully man experienced and understands.

“*For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin*.” **Hebrew 4:15**

And so, Jesus wept. And then raised Lazarus from the dead.

It's one of the most beautiful stories of His ministry on earth, and as Martha testifies her faith that her brother shared, that he shall rise again in the resurrection of the last day. Jesus expounds on this with the full Gospel, yet again:

*I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.*

Martha confesses the truth of the Gospel Jesus gives, the truth her brother and sister also believe. That those who believe on Him shall never die, but he shall live. This is salvation by faith and eternal security, yet again. 11 chapters in and in every one so far, this is the good news as given by Christ.

If you doubt His word is true, I don't know what else one could say to bring you to believe.

teachings.title: None shall pluck them out of my hand
teachings.summary: Jesus plainly says His believing sheep have eternal life and shall never perish, held in His and the Father's hand, so once saved is always saved.
teachings.text:
Jesus says "*My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one.*"

Like we have seen repeatedly, Jesus spells it out and explains His parables and analogies in clear, unmistakable language. Those who hear the Gospel and believe the truth Jesus gives **eternal life**. They **shall never perish**. No man can take them, that is make them unbelievers, bring them to repent of their faith, having repented into belief. **No man**. Not ourselves, not another. Once you are saved you are always saved, always His, always His sheep.

And in case you had any doubt about it, you're not only kept in Jesus' hands, but also God the Father's, who is greater than all. Who created everything, through Christ, who gave up His Son to save us, in Christ, and no one, no force, no act, nothing, can pluck us from His hand.

Jesus and God, His Father are one.

And the Jews not being His sheep cannot hear His voice. They cannot come to believe.

And so they took up stones to kill Jesus.

teachings.title: I will in no wise cast out
teachings.summary: John 6:37-40 refutes both Calvinism, since every one who sees and believes may have life, and loss of salvation, since Christ loses none given Him.
teachings.text:
The preaching Jesus gives that follows is so important, let's look at it again:

*37 All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.*

*38 For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.*

*39 And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.*

*40 And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

These verses are often used by Calvinists to say the Father chooses who is saved, but as we see in v40 *everyone* could see Jesus and believe. Not everyone will.

Those who say you can lose your salvation ignore that Jesus says those given Him by God's grace shall in no wise be cast out. That He **shall not lose any** who believe and are given Him. That they will have everlasting life and be raised up on the last day. **Everlasting**. You cannot lose your salvation.

Finally we have those who say you have to do the will of the Father to be saved, which is true, but they take it to mean obeying the commandments, repenting of all sin. But that is not the "will of the Father" Jesus teaches. He says His Father's will is that all who believe have everlasting life. To obey the Gospel. To accept His word.

teachings.title: Judas was a devil, never saved
teachings.summary: Judas does not show salvation can be lost, because Jesus knew from the beginning he believed not and called him a devil.
teachings.text:
*But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him*

There is a false doctrine out there that Judas proves you can lose your salvation, but of course that's untrue. Not only wasn't Judas saved, he was a reprobate and Jesus knew this. I've had people say to me "What? Did Jesus make a mistake choosing Judas? Clearly Judas believed and then rejected Christ and lost his salvation." But they speak in ignorance because they do not know the scriptures.

*Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil? He spake of Judas Iscariot the son of Simon: for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve.*

This literally couldn't be any clearer and is completely spelled out, And yet when showing this verse to people who deny once saved always saved, they cannot, and I mean this as a supernatural phenomenon of having their mind darkened in their eyes blinded, they **cannot** see this.

teachings.title: Remove thy candlestick is not losing salvation
teachings.summary: Revelation 1:20 says the candlesticks are the churches, so Christ's warning to remove a candlestick means a church's standing and fellowship, not a saint's salvation.
teachings.text:
Someone in the ApeMountain chat was asking about the verses in Revelation 2 and 3 where Jesus tells John about His issues with the 7 various independent churches. The question was basically aren't those verses where Jesus tells the churches to repent or He will "remove thy candlestick" saying they are going to lose their salvation?

The answer is a resounding no. As the Bible makes clear in **Revelation 1:12-20**, the candlesticks represent the churches themselves and their fellowship and blessing with Jesus:

*12 And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks;*

*13 And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.*

*14 His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire;*

*15 And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters.*

*16 And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.*

*17 And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last:*

*18 I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.*

*19 Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter;*

*20 The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

There's a myth that the dark sayings in Revelation are mysterious, but frequently when John seems confused or unsure Jesus or an angel will say "here's what this means." Obviously some remains through a glass darkly, but much of it is explained.

When Christ says "*Repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick,"* He is literally speaking of their authority, hedge of protection, etc, as His church in fellowship with Him. He doesn't threaten those saints with damnation, because that would contradict the Gospel given that led them to being God's servants.

Jesus repeatedly says something like "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches" in His letters to these churches. Far too many do not have an ear to hear.

teachings.title: Our flesh sins, not the new man
teachings.summary: Honest confession brings forgiveness through Christ's blood, and sin is not imputed to the believer because it is the flesh that sins, not the new man born of God.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 51**, having established the context and getting the contention on the false doctrine of original sin guilt that comes from a shallow reading of the text, we see the purpose of the Psalm is the honest confession of a righteous man.

David is not placing the blame of what he has done on anyone else, and accepts full responsibility for whatever God judges against him. His fear of the Lord has led him to Godly repentance and reconciliation.

*Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom*.

This is the meekness and honesty about our sin that God seeks, that in it, we can actually learn from Him and grow.

We discussed in the previous **Psalm 50** study that God doesn't seek the sacrifices and burnt offerings, but a meek and contrite heart. He is pleased as a Father when we come to Him for restitution and forgiveness. His mercy and grace are limitless, all He asks for is honesty in our heart.

*For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.*

David confesses, and calls upon the Lord to purge him with hyssop, the sponge like plant that was used to apply the blood on the posts during the first passover, the same that was present when the Lord was crucified and they gave Him gall to drink.

The washing of forgiveness by the blood of Christ is ours, that we become white as snow.

**Isaiah 1:18**
*Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.*

David pleads to be made to hear joy and gladness, to be cheered by the power of God's word to heal the brokenness he feels from the Father's chastening.

He asks God to hide His face from David's sins. To see them and remember them no more. To blot out his iniquity.

We know as saved Christians that this promise of God, to forgive our sins past, present and future, that He will remember them no more and place them as far from us as east is from west, is our blessed hope in the redemption that is found in Christ.

We take comfort in this truth when we are faithful to confess to Him;

**1 John 1:7–10**
*But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.*

This promise shows not only the faithfulness of God to forgive, but also that our sin in the flesh is not held against our ledger in Heaven. It is not imputed against those that are in Christ.

**1 John 3:9**
*Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.*

John is not contradicting himself by saying if we say we have no sin, we are liars and simultaneously saying we cannot sin, being born of God.

He is describing the same feelings from the failure of the flesh David writes about here.

When we sin, it is not the new man, created in Christ, but the flesh.

**Romans 7:15–17**
*For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.*

Our flesh sins. If we deny that we are liars. But by being born again in Christ, we do not sin. The difference is that the flesh, which we can mortify to sin, and restrain from our lusts, is dead. Nailed to the cross with Christ.

**Galatians 5:24–25**
*And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.*

teachings.title: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation
teachings.summary: David was not afraid of losing salvation but sought restored joy; God runs to the returning prodigal and wants a broken and contrite heart, not penance.
teachings.text:
Our spirit is quickened and covered by the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. It is His righteousness that covers our transgressions and the Spirit that seals us unto redemption.

So David, in his sorrow and remorse reminds God of this truth, and by doing so, reminds himself.

*Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy Spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit.*

David is not writing that he is afraid to lose his salvation, but seeking the confidence in it again that has been marred by his transgressions and the fear from the chastening he has received.

He is seeking to renew his relationship with God through his confession and appeals to mercy.

And the purpose? Is it to selfish ends of not wanting to feel guilty and to get back on the blessings side of God? No.

*Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.*

It is the mercy God shows us as His children that leads us to share His praise to others, that the lost see His light upon us and they glorify Him in Heaven. It is not only the wrath that leaves the world without excuse, but the peace that passes understanding we are given by getting right with the Lord.

When He delivers us from our guilt, forgiving our sin, restoring our relationship as sons, we cannot help but sing aloud of His righteousness.

The sinner who trusts Christ is celebrated in Heaven by all the hosts of God...

**Luke 15:7**
*I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.*

...How much more the prodigal son who returns to his Father?

**Luke 15:18–20**
*I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.*

The Father runs to meet his returning son, showering him with love. Before any confession of guilt or offer of penance or anything other than turning back towards God, the Father goes to him in comparison and restitution of their relationship.

God wants to forgive us more than we want to be forgiven. And we rejoice in His grace, that we may shew forth His praise.

Again, God doesn't want sacrifice. He doesn't want our works of penance and vows to change. He takes no delight in the ritual formulas of burnt offerings, and performative acts of contrition.

*The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

It is the healing of a loving relationship that He wants for us. Even at our lowest, we should remember this, and turn to Him again.

It is then, in reconciliation and peace with God, through Christ Jesus our Lord, that the works we do and the praise we sing will please Him. Then will our religion match our hearts, in healing and in service to the mighty God. Amen

teachings.title: David's cry of contrition
teachings.summary: Psalm 51 shows how a believer under God's judgment should come in humble worship and confession, trusting that God is faithful to forgive and cleanse even sins like David's.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51** is the clearest and most sober cry of contrition and supplication for forgiveness by a believer, in the face of a judgment by the Almighty God, that we have in Scripture.

It is David at his lowest. "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba."

We know the story. David doesn't go off to war as kings were expected to. He stays at his place and sees Bathsheba, the wife of his soldier, Uriah the Hittite, bathing on her nearby roof. Filled with lust, he has her. And as a consequence of that adultery, David conspired to have Uriah killed in battle, and wed his pregnant widow.

Nathan confronts the King, and the Lord curses David for his sin;

**2 Samuel 12:7–10**
*And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul; And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon. Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.*

The judgment of God was given, the child should die.

**2 Samuel 12:14–15**
*Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die. And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.*

David fasts and prays and stays by the child's side, but in the end the illness takes the boy.

**2 Samuel 12:18–19**
*And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.*

David, devastated, cleans himself and goes into the house of the Lord to worship. It is in this context that this Psalm was written.

Rather than a root of bitterness against the judgement of God, as many are tempted to take on in the face of such fierce judgement, David concedes and comes to the Lord, asking for mercy. As he has so often in **Psalms**, he begins in worship, praising God for His lovingkindness and mercy. Reminding himself, and the Lord of His great qualities, and appeals to the ultimate judge to blot out his transgressions.

This is a formula of prayer that we should commit to our prayer life. Under better circumstances and joyous events, or in grave repentance and regret for whatever sins we have committed, the Lord should be approached in humility and meekness of spirit. Hallowing His holy name.

The request is to forgive the confessed transgressions, knowing He is merciful and faithful to forgive His children.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

This same promise applies to believers, today. The sure knowledge that our heavenly Father is faithful to forgive us, even the sins of the level of David. To wash us throughly, to cleanse us. To blot the iniquity from our record, and heal us, and our relationship with God.

But note, it is if we confess our sins. David acknowledged his transgressions. We cannot lie to God and we should not lie to ourselves. We cannot hide from our sin when we've faced judgment, and our conscience keeps the sin ever before us in guilt.

teachings.title: Against thee only have I sinned
teachings.summary: David confesses his sin against God and owns that God's judgment is right, while those who resent God's judgment are destroyed by bitterness.
teachings.text:
The joy and benefit of the forgiveness of God comes in relief from that burden, and removing the fear of chastening, that comes from a contrite heart seeking His mercy.

*Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight...that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.*

David confesses that it is the transgression towards God that out him in judgment, and so he admits to God that not only has he sinned against Him, but that David acknowledges his understanding that God's judgments are right and deserved.

Again, it is very common to see people in sin, when facing the judgment of God for it, to grow to resent Him and despise His judgements. To make excuses for their acts, to deny their intent, to place what has resulted from their wicked ways on the shoulders of a God whom they reject as judge.

These people are destroyed with their bitterness, wracked with guilt, have a broken relationship with the God that bought them, and are often called home early, the result of their being incapable of being honest and appealing to His mercy.

But David shows us the better way.

teachings.title: David's repentance versus Cain's sorrow
teachings.summary: Unlike Cain, who only grieved his punishment, David as a saved man grieves his sin itself, and confession and a plea for mercy are the only way out of the Lord's chastening.
teachings.text:
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Loving God. The Lord's chastening can be fierce, and our wish should be to acknowledge our wrongdoing, and fear God.

Recognizing the predicaments we may find ourselves in are our own making, and calling upon the Lord to help is the only way out of whatever we have fallen into. Whatever snare we are caught in. Whatever arrows the Lord sends our way as a wake-up call, there is no relief except confession and a plea for mercy from the longsuffering God of our salvation.

In **Genesis 4**, we find Cain being cursed with punishment from the Lord for the first murder, the blood of Cain's brother, righteous Abel, and he says to the Lord;

**Genesis 4:13**
*And Cain said unto the LORD, My punishment is greater than I can bear.*

There was no remorse for what he had done, just sorrow at the consequence. But David paints the picture of a repentant sinner, recognizing that the punishment must be just, because it comes from God.

*There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin.*

Where Cain went about his day, and lied without a qualm when asked of God about Abel; *Am I my brother's keeper?*

In contrast, David, as a saved believer, has become unable to rest because of the guilt his sin carries. It is his iniquities that are the burden he cannot bear.

Faced with his sin and the consequences, it is David's sin that worries him more.

We should keep this perspective. To not go the way of Cain. Notice too, that rather than seeking healing and relief from the punishment by confession and having a contrite heart, Cain's concern is for his own life. God leaves a mark on Cain to ensure he lives and suffers for it.

But we who are His are commanded to hate iniquity. Even our own. Especially our own.

**Romans 12:9**
*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

**Proverbs 8:13**
*The fear of the LORD is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate*.

David sees the wounds caused by his sin as festering and infected, stinking. Literal or metaphorical, we all see the damage of sin in our lives. The harm it's caused.

We may not be spared the consequences, but we need not continue in the chastening that comes with unconfessed sin.

The loathsome disease that rots our flesh, that makes us feeble and sore broken. The disquietude of our hearts. This may be spiritual, it may be in our soul and how we feel, it may be the effect of sin in our bodies, literal and tangible.

Sin manifests in our hearts and in our bodies, and brings men to conviction when we fear God.

David, who in **Psalm 32** sang of the blessedness of the man whose sins are forgiven, covered and not imputed against them, is now singing of the wounds, failing strength, bitter loneliness as a result of his actions. Abandoned and betrayed.

In his sin, he has made friends with those that seek His life. He was deaf to their intentions. He did not speak up against them. Now he's between the reproof of God and the mischief of the wicked, and has no recourse but to seek the Lord.

*For in thee, O LORD, do I hope: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God.*

No matter how desperate our situation, no matter how foolish or wicked we've been, no matter the cause for our misery; be it the chastening of the Lord or the betrayal of those we've given breadth to do evil, the mercies of our Father, seeking His face and His grace, are always there for those who have trusted in Him. He has promised. God Who cannot lie. Almighty God. So we know we can turn to Him.

Because He is our hope. Because evildoers may magnify themselves in our failures. Because we are willing to admit we are helpless without Him. To come up halt, stumbling and falling, unable to go on. Sorrow continually before us.

Because we declare our iniquity, admitting our wrongdoing, being sorry for what we have done.

For these reasons, we can cry out to the Lord with confidence to deliver us.

teachings.title: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper
teachings.summary: With freedom to preach openly, Christians still hide, and believers must confess and forsake their sins, including neglect of church, Bible and soul winning, rather than harden their hearts.
teachings.text:
Moving on: When the righteous men rejoice, there is great glory. When God has blessed His people with leaders who openly praise His name, we have the opportunity for glory. But when the wicked men rise, the righteous are hidden.

Tying this again to soul-winning, evangelizing to the lost, praising God's name in the open, or even reading the Bible and speaking His word confidently, is easy in modern America, today. We have the freedom to openly glorify God. Our leaders, even if they are wolves and deceivers, pay lip service to the Lord and believers are able to openly proclaim Christ without fear.

Yet so many men are hidden, still. It's a shame that many churches do not have any soul-winning. That many Christians hide who they are, and what Jesus has done for them. That so few read the Bible here, while there are countries where reading scripture can be a prison sentence. That confessing Christ can end in death.

Maybe it is a parallel to the rich young man. That by our comfort and safety we grow complacent. Maybe revival requires tribulation. Maybe the embarrassment of riches we have in the freedom we've been granted by God has caused too many Christians to have their heart hardened for the lost.

Vs 13; *He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.*

We know that in Christ our sins are forgiven, past, present and future. But we are also to faithfully confess our sins to the Father, Who is faithful again to forgive.

Covering sin leads to the chastening of the Lord. Humbling ourselves to admit our failings will have mercy.

Keeping the theme going, you can see how those Christians who don't go to church, don't read their Bible, don't spread the gospel, would rather hide their sin than acknowledge and forsake them. If they confess, they're conceding to God that they know better, and if they agree that His way is the way forward, then they cannot continue on in theirs.

They become paralyzed by their own guilty conscience and love of their sin.

"If I go to church, I am admitting I should, and so now I am on the hook to keep going." Same with Bible reading, prayer, or evangelizing.

We read in vs 9 that if you hate hearing the law because you want to continue doing the things God says you shouldn't, even your prayers shall be abominations.

How much worse are our prayers when we have the liberty to go to church, to get plugged in, to hear hard preaching, to learn God's word, to hear the law and confess our sins and be forgiven, and have the freedom to joyfully tell others the riches of God, and yet we ignore it all?

Is it any wonder we end up with a wicked ruler will rise up over a spiritually poor people? To take away the things and riches we take for granted? To provoke God's people to turn again to Him and do what's right, that He may heal the land?

V 14-15 seem to be separate points, yet in this larger context they reveal a greater truth;

*Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief. As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.*

Don't harden your hearts. Humble yourself. Confess your sins, including those that come from omissions. To know to do good and to do it not. Return to the first love. Obey the Great Commission. We have been given the ministry of reconciliation, and the opportunity to be servants to the Lord. Don't squander it. Redeem the time. Repent, ask forgiveness and turn to the paths of the Lord.

teachings.title: The righteous are bold as a lion
teachings.summary: The wicked flee in guilt, but believers have boldness and a clean conscience by the blood of Christ to come to the throne of grace, while wilful rejecters face fearful judgment.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 28** continues the sayings of Solomon, recorded by the order of his 10th-generation grandson, King Hezekiah. And it begins with an often used saying; *The wicked flee when no man pursueth*...

The guilty fear the wrath they know they deserve. Constantly looking over their shoulder, and quick to defend themselves where no accusations have been made. Paranoia strikes the thief and the murderer, the habitual criminal lives in constant worry of being found out to the point they will expose themselves when there is no threat.

Parents are familiar with this behavior in guilty children. God is used to this in His children as well.

*but the righteous are bold as a lion.*

This boldness comes from having a clean conscience towards God by the blood of Christ;

**Hebrews 10:16-22**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin. Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; And having an high priest over the house of God; Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.*

For God treats us as His children, by faith in Christ, that when we sin, we have forgiveness.

**Hebrews 4:16**
*Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

We don't need to keep a guilty conscience, in constant anxiety. We have the boldness of Christ's righteousness and the promise of a merciful Father

The righteous don't despise the chastening of the Lord, or faint when we are rebuked of Him;

**Hebrews 12:6-8**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

But the unbelieving allow the fear of their guilt and unrighteousness overcome them, and their love of sin betray and snare them, they flee the throne of God to hide from His vengeance. Especially those that have heard His word and the instruction of righteousness, and have rejected it.

**Hebrews 10:26-27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

teachings.title: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy
teachings.summary: Denying our sin forsakes God's mercy, while confessing it, as Jonah did, is for our sake that we may know His forgiveness and cleansing.
teachings.text:
*They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.*

Don't deceive yourself when faced with chastisement of the Lord. Don't tell yourself lying vanities about your situation and the sin that led you there. God is long-suffering and merciful to a humble heart, calling out to Him. But you forsake mercy when you stay in denial.

For whatever else Jonah was, he did not deny his sin. He willingly gave himself up for the sailors on the ship. He admitted to God that he was lost without His mercy.

**1 John 1:7-9**
*But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

Confession of our sin to God is not for His sake, although a lying tongue is a thing that He hates. Confession, telling the truth in our heart about what it is we have done, what we do, is for our sake; that we may know His mercy and forgiveness and be cleaned from all unrighteousness.

Internalizing this mindset when it comes to your walk with God is a key to understanding and growing in faith.

teachings.title: The Lord hath put away thy sin
teachings.summary: When David confessed, God put away his sin so he would not die, yet chastened him in this life, a model for how believers get right with God.
teachings.text:
Here in **2 Samuel 12** the prophet Nathan is sent by the Lord to expose David's sin in taking another man's wife and doing it dishonestly through murder.

Nathan speaking the words of God tells David a parable of a rich man with abundant flocks who takes the poor man's only ewe. David is outraged at the story and demands the rich man be put to death for his lack of mercy, only to be told by the prophet that the rich man is the King.

The Lord knows our secret sin, and the things we are ashamed of will be revealed in due time. But God is also merciful, in that while we may sin and while we may face temporal punishment for it, He will not impute our sin against us, because we are justified in Christ.

*And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.*

We who are saved in Christ shall not die. Our sin has been put away by the washing of the regeneration given to us by the Spirit, by trusting in the blood of the Lamb.

But in this life we will be punished, that we may learn and the glory of God be known, not just by His mercy but His wrath. As an example for others.

And so the prophet tells the king that David's wives will be taken from him, and what he did in darkness will be done to him in broad daylight. That the Lord would raise up evil against him from his own house. And finally, that the son Bathsheba gave him will surely die.

David acknowledges his sin and understands his plight is of his own making, and ultimately accepts God's judgment against him. This is a model for us to follow. This is how we get right with God.

teachings.title: Confession: admitting our sin before God
teachings.summary: No one can be saved without confessing they are a sinner, and pride against confession is what drives people to works religion and false priestly confession.
teachings.text:
*And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing*.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*

Confession, the act of admitting guilt, of revealing your own faults and iniquities, is a fundamental act of humility in the Christian life. It is the realization that leads to repentance towards the Gospel, the understanding that yes, we have sinned before God and His standards are just and right, for He is holy, and we ask for mercy and salvation knowing in our hearts that we deserve death, for we have earned it. The wages of sin.

A soul that sins and doesn't confess their trespass to God, can't avail themselves of the sacrifice. You can't get saved without this acknowledgment. You can't accept salvation without knowing you need to be saved.

And as we covered in Romans; all men know. By the wrath of God revealed from heaven upon the ungodly. By the conviction of the holy Spirit, reproving the world. By the conscience we have, the law written in our hearts. So that we have no excuse. Everyone knows.

But few confess.

It is humiliating to be found out. It is one of the first sins we commit affirmatively, lying about something we have done. We seek to avoid punishment, but more so, our pride has us seek to avoid being exposed. Especially since so many sins are petty and embarrassing. Coveting. Lusts. All come from selfish and disgusting places. Admission that we aren't "good" is a hard nut to crack.

This pride and dishonesty, lying about sin to God, to others, even lying to ourselves, is the biggest stumbling block to accepting the Gospel.

Either a person will deny that God is real, that His judgments are right, that they aren't absolved by technicality, that the Bible doesn't *really* say that.

*Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?*

It is that lie that Satan uses to tempt us, from Eve on. And like Adam and Eve, hiding in the bushes from God, covering their sin with their own works, blaming someone else, even blaming God, as Adam did, we see the cope humans will cling to to avoid that humiliation of confession. Even before the eyes of God, in His presence.

This pride against confession is what draws people to a works-based false religion.

The idea that they are "good people" because they keep ordinances and receive sacraments, even the false half-hearted "confession" to a "priest," being absolved not by faith but by vain repetitions of prayer, given as punishment.

People seek to be absolved in any way possible short of actually acknowledging their sin.

And we see in our study of Leviticus, God provided the framework in the law that if anyone could follow it without falling short, they could theoretically be saved. It is the ultimate works religion, the only one God endorsed, and He did it to show that we need salvation in Christ. That all will fall short.

Even in the paradise of Eden, with one commandment only, man sinned.

We are given the law as a schoolmaster to bring us to the understanding that we need Jesus. And by the law, the understanding that to receive Christ we have to admit we need saving. That our righteousness is as filthy rags. That we sin, and God's judgment is just and right.

And so we must confess we are guilty under the law to be saved, and once saved, we confess our sins that God may work through the Spirit indwelling us to remove those thorns in our hearts.

We study the scriptures, and often learn that things we have done in the past were actually sinful. And like the Hebrews, once we have that knowledge we need to confess and seek atonement in faith through the Lord.

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.*

teachings.title: Confess your faults one to another
teachings.summary: True confession to God and to brethren is a God-given bulwark against sin, while false confession that excuses sin or works it off as penance is wicked.
teachings.text:
**James 5:16**
*Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.*

Brothers and sisters in Christ should edify one another, being of one mind in Christ. And that includes admitting our faults, confessing our trespasses with each other, and seeking prayer to help us overcome the flesh.

This is natural, normal and good.

The very act of a sincere confession to God is often enough to bring us out of the delusional rationalizing we do to cover our sins. And to tell others of our sin, knowing that it could be humiliating but for their love and grace, and their own humility in being an admitted sinner, is freeing. Knowing others are praying for your growth. These things provide a bulwark against sin. If your heart isn't deceiving you, it becomes more humiliating to stay in a sin than it is to fear being exposed.

True confession is a wonderful tool given by God that we may become separated unto the Gospel and better vessels fitted to His purpose.

False confession, anything that seeks to be given excuse or justification for our sin that we may remain in it, or that we can work it off in some way of penance, is wicked as Hell and leads people further and further into sin.

teachings.title: His mercies are new every morning
teachings.summary: A saved believer still carrying guilt should believe God's irrevocable promise that his sins are blotted out and remembered no more, and that it is never too late to turn back to the Father, whose mercies are new every morning.
teachings.text:
**Lamentations 3:22-23**
*It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.*

**Hebrews 10:16-17**
