*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

**Psalm 103:12**
*As far as the east is from the west, So far hath he removed our transgressions from us.*

**Isaiah 43:25**
*I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.*

**Romans 11:29**
*For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.*

Isaiah 38:17
*Behold, for peace I had great bitterness: but thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.*

If you are a believer, saved by faith in Christ Jesus and have been forgiven for your sins, and you still carry that burden of guilt, if you haven't given it to God to cast behind His back, to remove them from you as far as the east is from the west, to have your inequities blotted out forever, then please consider His word. Believe His promises, for they are without repentance. Irrevocable. He has promised to cleanse you of that burden, to redeem you as His sons.

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

No matter how backslidden. No matter how snared in sin. No matter how the devil accuses you before God, in Christ Jesus you are forgiven.

If you screwed up today, the Bible says that God's mercy is new every morning. We can choose to take up the cross again, to turn towards Him and do His will, every single day. To earnestly strive for the prize. To contend for the faith. To feed the new man and starve the old. To w*alk in the Spirit,* and not *fulfil the lust of the flesh.*

For a saved believer who has been sealed by the Spirit, it is never too late to turn to back to God and away from your sins. Like the Prodigal son, returning to the Father. And like that parable, the Father will rise to meet you, and celebrate your return. And your sin and inequities He will remember no more.

teachings.title: Full Assurance and Not Forsaking the Assembly
teachings.summary: Forgiven believers should not cling to guilt but draw near in full assurance and assemble together to provoke one another to love and good works.
teachings.text:
And so to those who live by faith, the burden of our sin borne on the cross by Jesus, quickened and sealed by the Spirit, made temples of God, adopted heirs, part of His priesthood, an holy people, we should have full confidence in the covenant and patience towards the day of redemption.

We shouldn't be miserable. We shouldn't cling to guilt for sins and inequities God has forgiven and remembers no more.

*If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

This is the liberty which is found in Christ.

And so, by implication Paul encourages us;

*Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

If we truly believe all of these truths and have faith in our salvation, then let us as brethren encourage and edify each other, and do good works with a clean conscience. Not selfishly trying to appease an angry God, not in dead works and fruitless sacrifices of bulls and goats, but as servants to the Lord who saved us. Free from the bonds of the law. Free from death and Hell. Out of the same grace and mercy shown to us by our Father.

It should be noted here that Paul encourages us, in the Spirit, to gather with other believers in an assembly for the purpose of building our faith and provoking each other to love and good works. Exhortation in the faith, especially as we see that day of Christ's return approaching.

This is an appeal to go to church. Note, not for salvation, not just because it's sin not to, not because you can lose your salvation if you don't. But like all good works, to the benefit of others and a reflection of the love God has shown us in our salvation.

Do not forsake the assembly, because by it we become more complete, more perfect and able to serve God better. And it will build your faith and patience, your knowledge of the Lord, bring blessings for your works as it brings more opportunities to serve others.

teachings.title: Forgiveness is not earned by penance
teachings.summary: Like Esau compounding his trespass to regain favor, we cannot earn forgiveness by penance; God forgives by grace and mercy those who sincerely confess and turn, as the prodigal son did.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 26**
*34* *And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:*

*35 Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.*

**Genesis 27**
*46 And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me*?

To catch us up, Esau, the oldest and heir by law to the inheritance of Issac, and by the blessing passed from Abraham to Isaac, heir to the promise of God, had sold his birthright to his younger twin, Jacob for a bowl of lentils. Jacob then, many years later, under direction of Rebekah, fooled Issac into also giving him the blessing.

Esau had also taken two wives of the Hittites, a heathen people of Canaan. This had greatly displeased their mother, Rebekah and Isaac.

And so Esau's anger at Jacob, a murderous rage, presented an opportunity; send Jacob away to Rebekah's people, Abraham's cousins, to find a suitable wife and return once Esau had calmed down.

And so, Jacob flees back to Padanaram, *to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughers of Laban thy mother's brother*.

Before leaving, Issac gives Jacob his blessing again, this time without guile or subterfuge.

*God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people; And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham.*

Seeing Issac blessing his brother, that he was sent to the daughters of Laban for a wife and knowing his own wives disappointed his parents, Esau tries to *work* to regain their favor by marrying a daughter of his uncle, Ishmael. Thinking this will help, but like most of our efforts to please people after making mistakes, it only compounds his trespass now having multiple wives.

Poor Esau, now Edom. We find in life, as well as before God, what others want isn't for us to "make it right" so much as to stop digging, and be sincere in asking for forgiveness. Penance isn't how we earn forgiveness. Forgiveness is given by grace and mercy, charitable love extended to a sincere change of heart and contrition, acknowledging what we've done and how it impacted others.

**Isaiah 1:18**
*Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.*

**Isaiah 55:7**
*Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

We see this idea of Biblical contrition and forgiveness in the parable of the Prodigal Son, who realizing his sin, turns back to his father, repenting of his decision to waste his inheritance with harlots and wine;

**Luke 15**
*18 I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,*

*19 And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.*

*20 And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.*

*21 And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.*

*22 But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:*

*23 And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:*

*24 For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.*

teachings.title: If we confess our sins
teachings.summary: 1 John is written to the saved: those claiming sinless perfection lie, and believers who confess their sins are forgiven and cleansed in Christ.
teachings.text:
First John, the epistle, is written to the saved. Here the Bible tells us if we the saved, want fellowship with God and one another, to walk with God, to confess our sins to Him, and be forgiven them all by Christ, washed clean in His blood.

But some claim sinless perfection, and believe what saves them is their not sinning. According to the Bible they are liars:

*7 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.*

*8 If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.*

*9 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

*10 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.*

In 1 John 2, he brings the point home:

1 John 2

*My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous:*

*2 And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.*

*3 And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.*

*4 He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.*

*5 But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him.*

*6 He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.*

*7 Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which ye have heard from the beginning.*

*8 Again, a new commandment I write unto you, which thing is true in him and in you: because the darkness is past, and the true light now shineth.*

*9 He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.*

*10 He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.*

*11 But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.*

*12 I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake.*

Note he is writing to brethren. To the children of God, babes in Christ. He is edifying them and encouraging them to walk with God, to avoid sin and not deny it, but understand that if we are honest we confess our sins, and they are forgiven already in Christ.

Because we are sons of God.

teachings.title: The way of the Lord is not equal
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 33 concerns physical judgment, not losing salvation; a backslidden believer's past works buy no pass from chastening, while a sinner who gets right is blessed.
teachings.text:
Following the parable of the watchmen, Ezekiel preaches a message to the people; repent and be saved.

The prophet preaches that if the righteous do wicked, are backslidden and not right with God, they will perish in the judgment of Judah. But if the wicked turn to God, restore their pledges and right their wrongs and walk in His statutes, they are forgiven. He shall not die during their tribulation.

*Yet the children of thy people say, The way of the Lord is not equal.* Man says it isn't fair that the wicked be saved by getting right, and their sins are no longer held against them, when their righteousness is forgotten with every sin. They say the Lord's judgment isn't fair.

*O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways.*

God's mercy on the sinner who repents isn't fair, it is grace. We all deserve worse. That Him for His grace.

The righteous sin, and think they are better than the wicked who sinned and gets right. This hypocritical judgment is iniquity. It's one of the things God hates the most.

This portion of **Ezekiel 33** is about physical salvation, with a spiritual picture for us today. Many make the entire message spiritual, and apply this to salvation, that you can lose salvation or that we must turn from our sins to be saved. But the context is the physical destruction of Jerusalem and her people.

The spiritual and practical application for believers is that we are His people, as saved Christians. We are Israel. And so, in this life, God will withhold His wrath and chastening to those believers who, however backslidden, come back to the statutes of life; the commandments. The way of the Lord.

While God's wrath is kindled against the backslidden believer who sins, despite their past righteousness.

In practical terms; if you are now living in sin - fornicating, lying, defrauding others, violent, hypocritical, covetous, worldly...or not in prayer, not reading your Bible, not attending church or soul-winning, it does not matter what works of righteousness you were doing before. They don't buy you a pass. You can't coast on "Well, I used to go to church and I used to go soul-winning. I did it for years!"

If you've stopped, you aren't right with God.

And if a greater sinner than you ever were, who never did those things in their life, starts today, they are more right with God than you.

And if you don't think that's fair, you are committing inequity. You are no different than the people who said the way of the Lord is not equal, who were destroyed by the Babylonians.

Again, this applies to chastening of believers. We are saved by grace through faith, not of ourselves. It is a gift of God.

But the blessings of this world come when you are right with God. And He withdraws His protection when those who call themselves by His name don't walk in His ways.

*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

If you aren't right, get right. Life is but a vapour. The time is now. Don't rest on your laurels, but press forward for the mark of a triumphant Christian life.

teachings.title: Chastening of the proud believer
teachings.summary: Like Nebuchadnezzar, a prideful backslidden believer may be chastened by God, even with mental affliction.
teachings.text:
One last point; God chastens whom He would, scourging every son. Too many Christians get comfortable in the blessings and protection God provides us. Like Nebuchadnezzar, we not only take things for granted, but begin to pridefully take credit for the things in our life that are by the grace of God.

He heard God's word and forgot all about it. He became prideful and paid for it.

I think mental illness is often from God, making us deal with the cognitive dissonance of our lies and self-deception and the truth of His word.

Don't be surprised if you continue down the road, backslidden, to have this type of punishment. I have both observed it and experienced a fraction of it. Don't let it happen to you!

teachings.title: The Lord hath a controversy with Judah
teachings.summary: Judah, representing the saved, still had sin God would scourge, but He calls His backslidden sons to turn to Him, keep mercy and wait on Him to be forgiven.
teachings.text:
The Lord is wroth with Israel, listing the sins of Ephraim, faithlessness, Idolatry, wickedness. But also with Judah;
*The Lord hath also a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways*.

If Israel are the unsaved and the reprobate, Judah, at this time, remained fairly faithful, and represents the saved. Keeping the legacy of the covenants with Aaron and David, the priesthood and the king. Not perfectly. As Jesus said to the churches in **Revelation 2 and 3,** *Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee*.

The Lord promises to scourge His sons. Judah and Israel, who started strong in Jacob, who fought to be first, grabbing Esau's heel, who wrestled with the angel and prevailed, who wept and made supplication in Bethel and *spoke to Us, Even the Lord God of hosts, the Lord is His memorial*, meaning Christ Jesus.

So God reminds Judah of His mercy; *Therefore turn thou to thy God: keep mercy and judgment and wait on thy God continually*. The same promise to the saved, who may backslide and be chastened. Turn back to the Lord and be forgiven.

teachings.title: Rehoboam humbled: the prodigal chastened
teachings.summary: Like Rehoboam, believers who backslide after early blessing are chastened by God, who warns them by His word, and the prodigal who returns finds mercy in the Father's house.
teachings.text:
Continuing the chronicles of Rehoboam as King over Judah, we see that despite his beginning fearing the Lord and obeying His words against their going to war with Jeroboam, and enjoying the blessings of his inheritance from his father King Solomon, and the blessings God had bestowed on him directly, Rehoboam turned his heart from following the Lord. And as the king went, so too the people.

And so God brought a challenge out of Egypt, to conquer Judah and put them in servitude.

The walled cities and stores came into the hands of Shishak King of Egypt. But before their utter destruction, as Jerusalem was surrounded and the king and his princess huddled there in fear, the prophet of the Lord came. Shemaiah preached to them that the Lord had forsaken them as they had Him.

Hearing this the king and his princes humbled themselves and got right with God, and while they suffered loss for their behavior, God showed mercy upon them.

Very familiar to a lot of Christians, who after conversion and with the support of those before them to edify them, do great things for the Lord and are blessed, but soon their passion dies and they turn from the path of righteousness. And God chastens them. But He is merciful to send His word as warning before destruction to get right with Him.

Many listen. We see many young Christians saved as children, blessed to be in a Christian home with parents raising them in the admonition of the Lord, who backslide entering into adulthood. They often lose the blessings they inherited, and suffer loss and the consequences of their sin, and chastened, hearing the word, get right with God and live out their days humbled, serving Him.

Some don't, and are destroyed.

If you have experienced this, and we're prodigal, you know the longsuffering and mercy of God, His forgiveness, and the regret of wasted time.

If you're in rebellion now, repent. You are always welcome in the Father's house, as sons and daughters. He will deliver you from what you deserve, that you may have a chance to serve Him.

The Lord is righteous. Amen

teachings.title: Delivered unto Satan, yet the spirit saved
teachings.summary: God uses Satan to chasten His people, and Paul's delivering the Corinthian fornicator to Satan for the destruction of the flesh that the spirit be saved teaches once saved always saved.
teachings.text:
This is a story of David we covered back during the study on 2 Samuel 24

The difference between the versions is slight, but the added detail gives us perspective. In **2 Samuel 24**, we are told;

*And again the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.*

Here, in **1 Chronicles 21** we get more understanding;

*And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel.*

Just like Job, often God uses Satan to tempt us that we may be chastened, corrected and brought to repentance or, sadly, fail and condemn ourselves further.

**1 Corinthians 5:4-5**
*In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.*

We see this in the case of the fornication going on in the church at Corinth, where a man among them is chambering with his father's widow. Not only fornication, but an abomination.

Paul tells them to church discipline him, that he be given over to Satan for destruction of the flesh, even if his spirit is saved. God allows Satan to destroy us in the flesh. The hope in church discipline is that the person gets right. Sees their error and comes back. But if not, at least in death they are free from the sin and present with the Lord.

Note this teaches OSAS.

Please follow the link to the previous study where I break down the sin of numbering the people in a way other than how God intended.

teachings.title: Saved but living in the old flesh
teachings.summary: A saved person can return to the old life since good works are not automatic, so we should disciple and encourage rather than doubt their salvation or condemn them.
teachings.text:
There's also a lesson here for saved Christians. Those who are the rocky soil, who receive the truth of the word with gladness and hope, but because they have no root in themselves, with her and die without producing fruit.

It is possible to receive the gospel and believe unto salvation and yet return to the same old life. Healed, washed, clean and reborn the way the Syrian Captain was, and yet living in the old flesh doing the same old things. Seeking pardon for not living the way you should, knowing that you've been forgiven.

Of course, if good works and sanctification came automatically with salvation, the New Testament wouldn't be filled with encouragement from the apostles to do good works. To pursue sanctification by walking in the spirit rather than in the flesh. To feed the new man rather than the old.

It's also why we are to disciple those that we help lead to Christ. Or to be edifying and supportive in the lives of those who we come across. Encouraging them to walk in the Spirit.

There are quite a few professing Christians and even entire denominations that teach that works come automatically, and without evidence of a changed life, we should doubt the salvation of someone.

While faith without works is dead, not being profitable to others, and we are justified before men by our good works, we should be careful to be understanding rather than judgmental. To encourage rather than condemn.

We have all been as Naaman, excited about the Lord and turning back towards the things that we were trusting in before. We should have some Grace and understanding for people who aren't where we are in our spiritual walk. Not to condone sin. But to not be confrontationally judgmental. Elijah could have lectured Naaman. But he told him to go in peace.

I think there's a lot that can be taken from that.

teachings.title: The covenant with David kept in Christ
teachings.summary: God's covenant of an everlasting throne was made to David, not to the Jews or any modern state, and is kept in Christ, yet its blessings are conditional and the saved are chastened when they sin.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **1 Kings**, and the reign of Solomon, we see that after 20 years, and much building and growth of his wealth and power, Solomon has completed the temple, and his palace and fortified Jerusalem and built up cities throughout Israel. He has been blessed by God, given tribute by many, gifts such as the city given by Pharaoh to his daughter, Solomon's queen. And through extensive trade and the loans and goodwill of the Phoenician King, Hiram (Huram in Chronicles), Solomon has made Israel a great nation.

But first he began with the Lord.

And so, 20 years after the first visitation of the Lord, God again appears unto Solomon, pleased with his faith and devotion. And He reiterated the covenant made with David, and to say Jerusalem is the place He has put His name, forever. That God's heart and eyes shall be upon it in perpetuity. The Lord says;

*And if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and my judgments: Then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Israel for ever, as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel.*

This covenant, that there shall be a king forever over Israel from David's lineage, is fulfilled in Christ Jesus. This is a personal covenant, not made to Jews or to the nation of the 12 tribes, or any modern state, but to David, and confirmed to Solomon, and kept in Jesus.

But the conditions of keeping the blessings that had so enriched Solomon and blessed the Temple he had built for the Lord, which He had hallowed for His name, were clear. That He would cut off the people if they or their children strayed, and the Temple cast out from His sight. Becoming a byword and an astonishment.

While Jesus rules over all things, forever the King of Salem, the blessings of that promise aren't without condition. We who are saved and become co-heirs with Jesus Christ, have the same understanding. That we, in this life are blessed by that promised King, and given eternal life and made sons of God, but we do not have a license to sin and disobedience is met with punishment and chastisements from our Father. Many a great Christian has fallen to this, backslidden and ruined in this life. Lacking proper fear of the Lord.

*Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold upon other gods, and have worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath the Lord brought upon them all this evil.*

Never forget the Lord that led you from spiritual Egypt. From the bondage of the law, to make you His people. To whom much is given, much is expected.

teachings.title: To whom much is given, much is required
teachings.summary: The men of Bethshemesh were punished more than the Philistines because they knew better, a warning that believers who know God's word are chastened more severely when they stray.
teachings.text:
*And he smote the men of Bethshemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even he smote of the people fifty thousand and threescore and ten men: and the people lamented, because the Lord had smitten many of the people with a great slaughter.*

While it is unclear how many Philistines died during the seven months of plague and evil done by the Lord, we know that of the city of Bethshemesh God slew 50,070 men for the temerity of looking inside the ark. They should have known better, who had the oracles of God and the Levites among them, to whom much had been given, but they allowed their own curiosity to get the best of them and so they were sorely punished.

**Luke 12:48**
*But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.*

We spend a lot of time rebuking false ways and warning those caught up in these apostate cults and damnable heresy of the Hell that awaits them if they don't repent, but it should also be a warning to us that know better. That our knowledge and understanding means that should we stray from the goodness of God, we should expect a much worse punishment for it.

**Hebrews 12:6-7**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

One could argue that the ignorance of the Philistines was a pain in their ass, but the willful sin of the men of Judah in Bethshemesh was far worse because of the expectation of understanding the Lord held against them.

A valuable lesson on obeying the commandments of God for a Christian.

teachings.title: Abraham's repeated lie and our struggle with sin
teachings.summary: Even Abraham repeatedly sinned from fear, so believers should judge humbly, knowing God saves by grace and chastens His sons for their good.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 20** tells a familiar story, Abraham and Sarah lying about being brother and sister while sojourning in another nation. We were just reading a similar account in **Genesis 12**, where they went to Egypt to flee a famine, acting out of fear, and compounding his sin, Abraham lied to Pharaoh about being married to fair Sarah. Here, they sojourn in Gerar, a nearby kingdom and their ruler, Abimelech sent and took Sarah, believing she was not married to Abraham.

We learn that this tactic, lying, wasn't a one-off, or even a two-off. Abraham actually tells Sarah:

*This is thy kindness which thou shalt shew unto me; at every place whither we shall come, say of me, He is my brother.*

Righteous Abraham. Father to us all who believe on Christ Jesus. Who with perfect faith believed God would spare or raise Isaac, whom he was prepared to sacrifice on an altar by faith. Great Abraham. And he struggled with sin and faith, repeatedly.

He lies, the Bible says, because she is fair (even elderly in years), and he believes that these nations he's sojourning in are godless heathens who would kill him as husband to take his wife. He leaves the land God gave him out of fear. In **Genesis 12**, fear of famine. And he concocts a lie about Sarah out of fear. And, at least twice, it bites him in the butt and God has to bail him out.

This should be a great lesson for us, especially those of us who aren't as righteous as Abraham. If he, a mighty man of faith, called "a friend of God," struggled with sin and fear. Who is embarrassingly caught in the same lie more than once, recorded forever in the preserved word of God, then we can know the same is true of us.

We all have sin in our lives that we struggle with. It is different for each person, and at various times in our life. Some old sins we conquer with the help of God's word and the Spirit within, while others we may pick up a long the way.

*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.*

*If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.*

We shouldn't be puffed up in our righteousness, hypocritically fruit inspecting other believing Christians to compare our own righteousness against theirs. Because we all sin and our righteousness is as filthy rags, the Bible says. But by grace are we saved, and the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ covers us all.

This doesn't mean to not judge, but to judge while understanding our own failings. Showing mercy and grace as God has shown us.

If Abraham struggled with fear and dishonesty, at certain times and situations, understand that we too likewise struggle.

But we can also see that God saves us regardless of our fear or lack of faith. He chastises those he loves and scourges every son. He often will expose us to embarrassment and humiliation in exposing our sin. But it is to our benefit, as it is here for Abraham.

teachings.title: The Lord also hath put away thy sin
teachings.summary: Nathan's word to David shows a saved man whose sin is not imputed, yet God still chastens His sons on earth, sometimes harshly.
teachings.text:
There is a lot going on in this verse, but I wanted to focus on something, where Nathan the prophet says to David, after ripping face on him and his sin, he says "*The Lord also hath put away thy sin*." It's a faint assurance, that God won't kill him dead for his murder of Uriah and adultery with Bathsheba. But it's also a statement of David's being a saved son of God, who's sins are not imputed. Who shall not die, but have eternal life.

We are punished here on earth for our sins. *For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.* Sometimes very harshly. Sometimes with death.

And so God punished David, yet He put away David's sin, because he had the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ. His faith in God's word.

teachings.title: Ananias and Sapphira: chastened unto death
teachings.summary: Ananias and Sapphira were saved church members, and their deaths show not lost salvation but that God scourges His own children for sin, even unto death.
teachings.text:
Acts 5 picks up immediately following the last verses of 4, where the gathered believers of the assembly had just praised God in Jesus name, and been filled with the Holy Ghost to preach the scriptures boldly. They had all things in common, meaning they shared possessions as needed, forsaking materialism to edify the church and do great things for the Lord. One disciple, Barnabas had just sold property and donated the sum to the church at Jerusalem. Likely to praise and blessings. And so we meet a married couple, Ananias and Sapphira.

Ananias and Sapphira, in the context of seeing Barnabas coveted his praise and honor in the church, and having land themselves to sell, sold it for a sum, but presented to the Apostles a lesser amount, keeping a portion of the proceeds for themselves while saying they gave all of it to the church.

Peter, by the Holy Ghost calls out Ananias, who is present before them presenting the gift. Peter says he knows that it's not the full total, and asks why lie to the Holy Ghost about it considering they weren't required to sell the land at all, or to give any of the money to the church. They had every right to give a portion, as it was theirs to give.

But the lying for praise and to be favored among the congregation is the problem, and confronted, Ananias collapses dead at Peter's feet.

The brothers bury him, and a few hours later, as they are putting him in the ground along comes the wife, Sapphira.

Peter gives her a chance to be truthful, and she sticks to the story her and her husband had concocted. Peter, again in the Spirit curses her to the same fate of her husband, striking her dead. The gathered now know Ananias' death wasn't just happenstance, but that the couple has been punished by God.

Were Ananias and Sapphira saved? Didn't they just feel the presence of the Holy Ghost when the church prayed the chapter before? The Bible says in Acts 4 that the entire church was of one heart and one soul. They were of that church. I think the implication is clear they were.

But their being in Heaven when they die, justified by faith and Jesus' imputed righteousness didn't keep them from sinning, nor did it stop God from punishing them with their lives.

Many of the religion of works, who maintain that you must repent of sinning to be saved, and claim that the Gospel of Christ, salvation by faith in grace, is a "license to sin." And so, being fruit inspectors, take this story as evidence they were not believers. But what it shows is that God chastises His own for our iniquity. He takes the rod to His children when they sin. The Bible says He scourges His adopted sons and daughters. Even unto death. We saved are held to a higher standard than the unsaved, and we are punished here in this earth, sometimes more so than the unsaved, who are not God's children. This is why we should walk in the word, live for God, take up the cross and follow Jesus. Honoring our heavenly Father, which brings blessings upon blessings.

It is an amazing gift to be given a chance by God to bless others, to help people. To give freely what we have to others in the church in need. But our own pride and greed can often stop us from receiving the blessings, and instead lead us to chastisement in our sin.

teachings.title: The only surety we can count on
teachings.summary: Being surety for others brings regret, but the only sure surety is God's, the Holy Spirit as the earnest sealing the believer's inheritance by Christ's finished work.
teachings.text:
*He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.*

In **Proverbs 6**, we saw Solomon warning against surety, for a friend or a stranger, and here we see a similar warning. The seeming contradiction, that one who disfavors backing another's debts is seen by God as more sure than one who gives their pledge for a stranger. That they will regret it.

The only surety we can count on is God's. In scripture the Holy Spirit is described as the "earnest" or seal guaranteeing a believer's eternal inheritance and salvation. The surety of our eternal life.

**Ephesians 1:12-14**
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Because our surety is covered by the finished work of Christ, and sealed by the ernest payment of the Spirit, we can count on it.

But for the stranger, we shall smart for it.

teachings.title: Christ our surety, the Spirit our earnest
teachings.summary: The law of vows and surety pictures salvation, where Jesus is the surety of a better testament and the Spirit the earnest until the day of redemption.
teachings.text:
The last chapter of Leviticus, the law of the vow, offering and tithe. These are the general conditions for the sake of clarifying what goes into the surety of a vow or, rather the amount held until completion of the vow, that could be redeemed upon completion, or the case of land and other things offered to the priesthood outside of what is proscribed earlier, for the sake of a special promise to God.

It is an idea later corrupted, where we see Jesus in the Gospels call out the Pharisees for allowing an adult son to place his things in such a vow, to avoid his responsibility to honor his father and mother, caring for them in their old age, or "Corban."

*But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.*

The idea of temporarily giving or using collateral to ensure keeping of a vow before God, and redemption, is reflected in salvation, where Jesus is offered, the vow made, the Spirit serving as surety until the day of redemption.

**Hebrews 7**
*18 For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.*

*19 For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.*

*20 And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:*

*21 (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)*

*22 By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament*.

And

2 Corinthians 1
*19 For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.*

*20 For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.*

*21 Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;*

*22 Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.*

*23 Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.*

We see these examples of promises of God are made with an application of earnest, the surety of a vow. The blood of a testimony. Redemption at the day appointed. To be paid in full as God vows. He gave His word.

This concept of contractual law is the basis of everything God does. And why He detests bearing false witness, perjury, false weights and measures, cheating and stealing...It is ultimately why salvation is by faith accepted by believing a witness testimony, the Gospel shared by a believer. Why we must be blameless, that in judgment a man may trust our confession of faith. And it is why we see the emphasis in the law of trusting multiple witnesses who testify of the same thing. It's why we have 4 Gospels.

*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

And Jesus saying; *If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true. There is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.*

The Bible is, regardless of anything else, the testimony of God to His promises, and faith is believing He is true.

God's word. Not the words of God. If that makes sense.

And we can believe His vow, that we will be redeemed, after He gave his Son as surety and the Spirit as earnest. Amen

teachings.title: The earnest of our inheritance
teachings.summary: The Holy Spirit is God's earnest, sealing believers as His purchased possession until the redemption of the body.
teachings.text:
*O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

**Romans 7** explains the war within the saved between the spirit and the flesh, that the flesh worketh the law of sin, while the Spirit worketh the law of God. That our flesh has us do what we would not. And not do what we would. That our temporal bodies are in a battle with the new man, the quickened spirit within us, the Spirit of God that resides in our hearts.

But that if we walk after the Spirit, we will do the things of God. But if we walk after the flesh, we will go after the lusts of the flesh.

But we are delivered from this mortal body. The promise of God is that as we receive the Spirit as the earnest of our adoption, that the day of redemption is when it is fulfilled with a glorified body, unto eternal life and without the temptations of the flesh.

**Ephesians 1:12-14**
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Earnest is money, sometimes called a “good faith deposit,” is a sum that is included with your offer to purchase something to show your seriousness of intent to go through with the purchase, which is also called redemption. The Spirit is the earnest of God, given in Christ, sealing us as His until the resurrection, whereby we are redeemed.

**1 Corinthians 6:20**
*For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.*

teachings.title: The Spirit beareth witness
teachings.summary: The Spirit witnesses that we are children and joint heirs, so even when the flesh fails we know our eternal state and should rejoice rather than despair.
teachings.text:
And so, back to Romans, Paul is offering the hope we have, while yet in sinful flesh, that we have been purchased with a price, the blood of Christ, and adopted by God as heirs in faith. To be delivered upon at the day of His glorious coming.

Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh...The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the Children of God.

If we are children, then heirs of God, joint heirs with Christ. The kingdom is ours, as princes of it. Wherein are many mansions prepared for us. Glorified bodies that have no want of need or corruption. The streets, paved with gold. Given rewards for our faithful service.

But, here on earth, we still are in the flesh. And if we walk not in the Spirit, the lusts of the flesh will we do. And that is often frustrating and depressing for we who are saved.

O wretched men that we are.

But Paul, writing in the Spirit says hey, it's ok. We will be saved out of this condition. You have the Spirit testifying within you. You know you are saved. Sealed. And that the sufferings of this life are nothing in comparison to the glory of the life to come in Christ. If we are tempted and successful in mortifying our members, if the Spirit working in us brings us from sin, we may suffer for God, but to glory everlasting.

And if we fail, and sin and the flesh dies, we still have eternity in the same glory, that this temporary condition will be no more. So rejoice, rather than despair. We are not like those that don't believe. We know for certain our final condition. And so we walk in the Spirit that we may not do the things of the flesh, that we may serve God and store up treasure in Heaven through works worthy of those adopted sons.

teachings.title: The epistles are written to the saved
teachings.summary: Paul writes as one saved to fellow saints, so the epistles are to the saved, and false churches that call assurance the sin of presumption have another gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing Romans 1, Paul having introduced himself by his relationship to God through Christ, and stipulating the faith shared by believers unto salvation, he addresses the Roman saints, thanking God through Christ (our prayers to the Father are in the name of the Son), that the Roman churches are world famous for their faith. That Paul prays for them and to be among them, without ceasing. (Note this isn't in vain repetition. It just is his saying it is frequently an ask he makes)

Paul says that he, as a servant to the gospel, the shared faith he previously stipulated, and as a minister to it, that he serves God with his spirit in the gospel of the Son, and calls God to witness his sincerity to the readers. This is a letter, and Paul wishes to convey earnestness that may not be discerned from text alone.

Paul's prayer is by the will of God he may have a safe and prosperous journey to them. All prayer should be to the understanding that God's will be done.

Paul himself longs to see them, that he may impart unto them some spiritual gift, that he may be used of God to be a blessing, or to edify the brethren there. And that he himself would be blessed, given comfort being with them by the mutual faith they share.

This is important to understand, it is why Paul began his letter this way, emphasizing what that faith is, in Whom, to what end, and that it is what joins him to these strangers half a continent away.

All epistles are written to the saved. They follow the Gospels in the Bible, because it is understood that by the testimony of them we would come to believe and accept the gift of salvation, eternal life in Christ Jesus, given by God's grace.

Most apostate religions claiming Christianity as their source, frame the epistles as written to the world in general. Not to the saved, because they teach that man can never know if they are saved or not. Because they teach works-based justification, they have another gospel.

But as Paul says here, *that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.* Paul is clearly saved, he is writing to brethren of their shared faith. They are saints. Forgiven in Christ. Just as we are saints today, if we've been born again in faith.

The naysayers today in the false apostate churches would charge Paul with the "sin of presumption," for assuming he is saved, let alone assuming others are.

Paul continues, writing that he intended to come to them in the past, but was "let hitherto," led to where he is now at that writing. He intended to come to Rome before, (and God will grant him this soon enough, though not as Paul might think, but rather as a prisoner for the faith), that he could bear fruit in the city that is the seat of power for the empire. That he could get people saved by the Gospel, even as he has among the other Gentiles, the other nations of Asia Minor where he had traveled.

He says he is a debtor to the Greeks and Barbarians, that is the people of the empire, of Macedonia, and to the nations considered barbarians, not of the formal Greco-Roman people, and to both the wise and unwise, the civilized and educated and the simple peasants, all of whom Paul has had great success in bringing to Christ. This has him excited to preach the same Gospel in Rome, to win souls.

It is here, Paul having established all these things, reemphasizes once again the Gospel he is a servant to, that he begins to transition from introduction and stipulations to the meat of the arguments he, in the Spirit, will make.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth*.

The power of God unto salvation comes from the Gospel. The Gospel is as he has stipulated, that God the Father gave us His Son, who died and rose again, to fulfill the scriptures, given by the prophets, wherein He promised a redeemer. Faith comes by hearing the word of God. The preaching of the Gospel is being a servant of the Lord.

teachings.title: Blessed is he not offended in me
teachings.summary: John's doubt was answered by the works Jesus did, showing it is fine to seek confirmation of our hope but we must believe the report and not be ashamed of the gospel.
teachings.text:
And so this act, and others like it, begin to be spread throughout the land. All of Judea hears the rumors of Christ; *That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.*

And hearing this word go out, many come to faith. Yet others find their faith shaken and tested.

John the Baptist, in prison for his preaching of repentance at the coming of Christ, hearing these things. In bonds, separated from the outside world, probably feeling occasional despair. Doubt.

And so hearing of these signs and wonders, John seeks to know; is Jesus the Christ as he believed? Is it his faith confirmed? Is it too good to be true? And so, he sends disciples to ask Jesus, directly. *Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?*

The Bible doesn't give us an immediate answer from Jesus. He doesn't tell them, He shows. That very hour Jesus heals infirmities and casts out spirits. Restoring sight to the blind.

Then Jesus answered. He says tell John what you have seen. Jesus doesn't argue His divinity or that He is the Christ. He lets His actions justify Him before man, that they may know and believe, and bring this good news to John. *How that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.*

His mission statement. The prophecy of Isaiah made real.

**James 2:22**
*Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?*

We are saved by faith alone. Justified before God in Christ. Not of our dead works. In much the same way, John's faith in Jesus being the Christ that he hoped for, that he believed in, is made perfect by the work Jesus did. By the witness and testimony of what those disciples had seen. His doubt assuaged, I am sure.

And Jesus adds; *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.*

Offended in the Gospels means shaken of faith. Turned aside from the correct path by shame or doubt or the behavior of another. By false teachings. And here Jesus is saying that we who aren't shaken, who are not ashamed of the Gospel, who aren't troubled by the truth of who Christ is and what He has done for us, are blessed. The antithesis of **Mark 8:38**: 

*Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.*

It is ok to have doubts. To seek a confirmation for the hope we have, but at the end of the day we are to believe the report. To trust God and His promises. To believe the witness of others, and to hear His word and have faith, unashamed.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.*..

teachings.title: Work out your own salvation is not doubt
teachings.summary: Work out your own salvation does not deny assurance, since Paul in the same epistle is confident God will perform the work He began in them by the gospel.
teachings.text:
Philippians is one of my favorite epistles, for it's clear meaning and beautiful prose. It is easily understood and straightforward doctrine on sanctification and doing works of the Lord.

However many works-based false teachers use the "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" line to teach that you cannot be assured salvation, and that we must do works to be saved. This out of context understanding is contrary to scripture, even scripture within the same epistle. In chapter 1 Paul says:

*For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now;*
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.*

He has confidence in them, that they partake in the same grace that saved him. This is only conditioned on their having fellowship in the same Gospel he preached to them, not on their works, and with not doubt that God works in them.

It is another case of reading the whole of scripture and comparing it with itself, saving us from bad doctrine.

teachings.title: Sealed unto the day of redemption, against false churches
teachings.summary: Believers are sealed by the Spirit with eternal life, and churches teaching you can lose or must earn salvation, or that they are the body, are false churches that cannot save.
teachings.text:
Note the doctrines here, that unity of faith into the body, where Christ is the head. That we are sealed by the Spirit, given eternal life, testified by the new man within us, that we may know and have confidence in our trust in God. This is the promise of salvation.

Denominations that teach you can lose your salvation, that you must earn it, that only they can give it, that they are the head and the body, teaching the vanity of the mind and tossing their members to and fro with every changing wind of doctrine, rather than standing fast upon the unmoving rock of the Word...these false churches cannot save. They are the bondsmen, keeping people in chains.

teachings.title: Sealed unto the day of redemption
teachings.summary: Once we believe we are purchased by the blood and sealed by the Holy Spirit as an earnest until God redeems us at the resurrection.
teachings.text:
Further, once we believe we are sealed by the Holy Spirit as the earnest, the down payment as it were, until redemption, where God makes good on His promise, on the day of the Lord.

Once you are saved you are purchased by the blood. To let you know God's promise is good, He sets the Holy Spirit to seal you, to quicken your spirit, to awake the new man inside, and that seal is until the day He redeems you. He makes good on the promise. He raises you from the dead in glorified bodies to inherit His Kingdom. It is a contract entered in to by faith with God by believing His testimony. Taking Him at His word.

teachings.title: Saved Christians believe the word
teachings.summary: The sure sign someone is saved is not lifestyle or commandment-keeping but that he believes God's word when it is preached, for God justifies by belief alone.
teachings.text:
If you want to know if someone is a saved Christian, the evidence isn't their lifestyle or their adherence to the commandments. The only sure way to know is if they believe the word of God. When they hear preaching that is from the Bible and don't recoil from it, but accept it. That they hear Doctrine expounded upon from the word and, knowing that scripture is inspired by God indicate that they believe God.

This is very difficult for people who were raised in false churches where they were trained to be hypocritical, Pharisees. Being fruit inspectors.

You may need to see change in someone to have them justified before you, because you're a respecter of persons. But to be justified before God one needs only believe his testimony and accept it as truth.

teachings.title: Godly sorrow versus the sorrow of the world
teachings.summary: Cain sorrowed over his punishment but never repented, while David's godly sorrow hated his sin and worked repentance.
teachings.text:
**2 Corinthians 7:9–11**
*Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing. For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death. For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.*

This exchange perfectly encapsulates the fundamental difference between the sorrow of the world, held by Cain, and the godly sorrow, expressed by David.

The burden Cain couldn't bear was the punishment, but he sorrowed not unto repentance. He never changed his mind about what he had done.

David's sorrow is godly, he cannot bear his own iniquity and hates his sin that brought him low, rather than resenting the punishment he'd received.

The difference between worldly sorrow that works death versus godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, being delivered from the scourging, the ancillary consequences and from the scorners and those that plot mischief, taking advantage of our broken and contrite state.

**Hebrews 12:11–13**
*Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby. Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.*

teachings.title: Repent ye: John the Baptist's call to believe
teachings.summary: Repent means to change your mind and believe, not to stop sinning, so those John baptized confessing their sins had believed and were saved, baptism being the answer of a good conscience, not its cause.
teachings.text:
Repentance Moment:
**Matthew 3:1-12**
*In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?*
*Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.*

Repent ye; for the Kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Repent means to change your mind, to accept new information as true and have a change of heart, a conversion.

Here, John the Baptist is saying "Reconsider what you know and believe me." He is not saying "get your life together and stop sinning, the Kingdom of Heaven is here." They were baptized in the water confessing their sins, because they believed him, and were saved.

While false gospels that add works to salvation may disagree, Bible believing Christians who know water baptism is an answer for a good conscience before God, and not the cause of it, should be able to understand this context.

John further chastened the religious leaders of the Jews, who came down to see him and his work, making the paths straight for the Lord. He asks them who has warned them to flee the wrath to come? Where are their followers come to be baptized before the coming of Christ? Where is their fruit meet for repentance? If they had preached the coming of Christ, they would have followers ready to accept the truth that the Christ was come. But this generation of vipers did not. They were trusting in being seed of Abraham.

The water baptism of repentance, the sign of believers, was a prelude for the baptism of the Spirit in Christ. A baptism of fire. Amen

teachings.title: The woman taken in adultery and spiritual adultery
teachings.summary: Jesus exposed the scribes' own adultery against God, and his go and sin no more is a call to repentance toward Christ, not to sinless perfection.
teachings.text:
With this perspective, the woman taken in adultery story from the Gospels, takes on added context:

**John 8:3-11**
*And the scribes and Pharisees brought unto him a woman taken in adultery; and when they had set her in the midst, They say unto him, Master, this woman was taken in adultery, in the very act. Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou?*

*This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not. So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground. And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst. When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee? She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.*

Now the scribes sought to test Jesus and make Him choose; either keep the law as they saw it, and stone the woman angering the Romans, or speak against the law, angering the Jews.

But as we know, Jesus simply said *'He that is without sin among you, cast the first stone.*"

The truth was they didn't bring her before Him in good faith, they didn't bring the man she had supposedly committed this crime unto death with, that he may face the same justice. But their real sin was their own adultery against God. The hypocrisy wasn't so much in their judgement of the woman, but in their unfaithfulness to the Lord.

And then Jesus, having shown them their own adulterous hearts, tells the woman to go and sin no more. Which spiritually, in that context of whoredoms against God, is a call to repentance towards Christ. (not a call to sinless perfection and works salvation)

teachings.title: Repentance from false beliefs about God
teachings.summary: What people most often repent of is not their sins but their false beliefs about God, His judgment and their own righteousness, turning from dead works and believing the gospel.
teachings.text:
And this ties into the renewed theme of the week; repentance.

The thing most people "repent of" isn't their sins. Most people know sin is bad and hate it and don't like themselves for it. These Jews in Jerusalem for the fast knew in their hearts they were in sin, just as people do today. They have a conscience and the Spirit convicting them, least they be reprobate.

What people most often repent of are the false beliefs they have about God. About His judgment. About their own righteousness or how they can escape punishment for their sins.

"Oh I thought idols would save me."
"I thought the law would save me."
"I thought maybe hell wasn't real."
"I didn't know my works weren't enough."

It's literally what they are being called to repentance from in NT scripture. The Jews thinking by their being Abraham's seed they were going to inherit the kingdom no matter what. That they could achieve their own righteousness by works of the law and keeping the traditions of men. That the Kingdom of Heaven was theirs on this earth. That the Messiah would be political. A man of war. That circumcision availed them.

The Greeks believed their dead idols and false gods, that they superstitiously bowed to and served, would save them. That God wasn't real. They worshipped the created more than the Creator who is blessed forever, amen.

Jews and Greeks alike didn't believe Jesus was the Christ. They sought a sign, and wisdom. But the power to be saved was in the word of God. The Gospel preached and believed. Repentance from dead works and vain traditions and towards God. Reconsidering the way to the Kingdom of Heaven, and believing.

Just as in Jeremiah's day. Just as it is today.

teachings.title: Godly sorrow and the Corinthians' repentance
teachings.summary: 2 Corinthians 7 shows already-saved believers repenting of sin after Paul's rebuke, and teaches that godly sorrow can lead to repentance unto salvation while worldly sorrow works death.
teachings.text:
Is there a biblical example of repentance from sin? Of turning from, with fresh information changing ones mind, turning towards the correct action in regards to stopping sinful behavior? Yes.

But it's not regarding getting saved (not directly), but of those who had already believed getting right.

In 1 Corinthians, Paul wrote to the saints in Corinth regarding the open fornication among them, and their taking one another to court for petty disputes, among other things. He ripped into them, that they ought to know better and to repent of it, to think better of it. To come to the realization that it is wrong and hurt their ability to do God's will in sharing the gospel, while they had such sin among them.

And in 2 Corinthians, written a year or so later, Paul tells us by way of praising them, that they had repented of it.

**2 Corinthians 7**

*4 Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.*

*5 For, when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.*

*6 Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;*

*7 And not by his coming only, but by the consolation wherewith he was comforted in you, when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me; so that I rejoiced the more.*

*8 For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.*

*9 Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.*

*10 For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.*

*11 For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.*

*12 Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.*

*13 Therefore we were comforted in your comfort: yea, and exceedingly the more joyed we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.*

Note in verse 10, Paul is giving us a general rule, that godly sorrow, that is sincerely being sorry at a wrong you've done, leads many to the repentance of belief that is salvation, while the sorrow of this world to death.

In other words, being sorry you were caught, sorry you're in trouble, sorry you're paying a price for it, sorry that God has chastised you, this is worldly sorrow, and in it is death, because it isn't genuine, it's selfish.

Paul says, godly sorrow, truly understanding the harm done to others or to God by our transgressions, can lead to repentance towards salvation, a change of mind that cannot be repented of. Faith in Christ, that cannot be lost once gained. Once saved, always saved.

But to the Corinthians, who had already tasted the good word of God, tasted the heavenly gift, and the powers of the world to come, partakers of the Holy Ghost, as they'd already come to repentance unto salvation. The Bible says, *it is impossible...to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

So Paul isn't telling the Corinthians that their turning from the sin he pointed out among them is how they were saved, for they were already, but makes this comment as a part of a larger point, regarding their acceptance of his rebuke.

teachings.title: Sorrow is not itself repentance
teachings.summary: Godly sorrow for sin is not repentance but one thing that can work it, and others come to repentance through compassion and the witness of believers, in tears or in joy.
teachings.text:
But to focus on this a moment, as it is the only clear verse on the matter of "repenting of sin" in regards to salvation, note that this sincere sorrow for sin is not itself repentance, but rather, repentance is the work of that sorrow. That some may come to understanding of the faith by which we must believe to be justified by the sorrow for those they have wronged and the life that they've led. The regret. The penitent believer.

Because, the Bible says of some, we *save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh*. Amen, this is the case of many, brought to repent unto Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and relief from the godly sorrow and guilt weighing their conscience, lifted up by the Holy Spirit and the surety of the promise.

But again, that's not the only thing that worketh repentance. *For some have compassion, making a difference,* our caring and meekness, our ready answer for our hope, our chaste conversation, our example, the light of Jesus Christ shining through us, bring many to repentance as well.

As many receive it in tears, many still receive the truth in joy.

The circumstance and situation, the seed planted, the watering, the harvesting, the condition of the soil and the time of the season varies. But the repentance, the acceptance of the truth and the salvation earned remains the same, in sorrow and tears, or in laughter and joy.

teachings.title: The fruits of godly sorrow
teachings.summary: Paul's list of carefulness, clearing, indignation, fear, desire, zeal and revenge shows the fruits of godly sorrow, useful both for getting right with God and for judging whether another's sorrow is genuine.
teachings.text:
There is more valuable doctrine on repentance of sin to be had in this chapter, the change of mind with new information from Paul's first epistle and realization by the Corinthians, that what were doing that was wrong. Their godly sorrow leading to their getting right with God. The accompanying signs of genuinely changing their minds. In chapter 11, Paul lists the ways by which he knows they truly were sorry.

Paul writes; *For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.*

He says this selfsame thing, this godly sorrow that may led one to salvation, is evident in them. He determines that they took his rebuke in the spirit it was intended and it manifested in their change of heart, which he sees (through the report of Titus), in that the rebuke and the sincere sorrow it caused led them to be *careful*; to take care and paying attention to the matter and the implications there of.
To a *clearing of themselves*, that is getting right, to strive for being blameless, in this and in other possible sin. The *indignation* they felt towards themselves, the outrage at their own failings. The *fear,* of the chastisement from God, and the natural repercussions of their actions. The *zeal, the vehement desire,* by which they sought to get right, *the revenge* they took upon themselves, making good on the restitution of their error.

These signs by which Paul acquits them, that *ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.*

This is a helpful list, both for those us us seeking to get right with God regarding sin in our life, and how we should act, and for judging rightly the sincerity, be it godly or earthly sorrow, of those who have wronged us and are seeking forgiveness and claim to be making amends.

Genuine godly sorrow and a turning from a sin, or sins should produce a carefulness surrounding the behavior, an understanding of what it is you've done, how it affects others, the ripple effects and implications for the harm you've caused, and the things that lead you to the sin, whatever it may be. Not giving occasion to the flesh.

It should lead to a clearing of yourself. An assessment of not just this particular sin, but of how you may be perceived by those around you, to whom you need make restitution, and others caught up in the wake of our iniquities. To make yourself as blameless as possible going forward, in careful consideration.

You should be indignant at what you've done. Outraged at yourself. Embarrassed by the shame, hating even the garment spotted by the flesh. Despising that about you that led to your sin.

And having a vehement desire and zeal for reformation, taking revenge against yourself, which here means making an honest retribution for the harm caused, not begrudgingly, but with zeal. Willingly and needfully making things right, as your vehement desire.

Now note again, these all are the fruits of godly sorrow, just as repentance is the coming to understanding, in this case through that sorrow. They are not the same thing.

teachings.title: Believers cannot apostasize, continued
teachings.summary: Sums up that believers cannot apostasize and apostates cannot believe, with Hebrews 6:7-9, and urges comparing scripture with scripture.
teachings.text:
TL:DR - Believers cannot apostasize and apostates cannot believe

**Hebrews 6:7–9**
*For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned. But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.*

Here, the Bible gives us the parable to explain the apostasy verses that came before it.

The same rains and earth are given to both the dressed fields that bring forth herbs also brings forth thorns and briers, rejected and cast into the fire.

This directly applies to those that tasted of the truth, but did not consume, who see the power of the Spirit but never trusted the truth. They are the thorns and briers. The saved are the herbs meet for the dresser (the fruit of those who won them to Christ). The ground that bears thorns isn't good soil that "lost" its status; it is bad ground whose true nature was finally exposed by the rain.

The parable explains the concept beautifully.

It does not say the herbs become thorns, let alone that briers eventually are turned to fruit.

And so Paul, having explained this concept, reassures the believers he is writing to.

**Hebrews 6:9**
*But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.*

The fundamental problem is that people accept things without actually comparing scripture with scripture, to see if the thing they are being told is so.

They don't have enough Bible knowledge to do anything but to regurgitate proof texts that they were given, that they accepted at face value. And worse, when presented with context of their proofs, that show that the cherry-picked eisegesis is wrong, and why, they just dig in their heels and act like fools.

Clowns.

teachings.title: Believers cannot apostasize
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 1, 1 John 2 and Hebrews 6 that the saved cannot fall away or believe a strong delusion, and that apostates never believed.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18–23**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

That which may be known of God is made manifest by His wrath revealed from Heaven. Man has no excuse.

Many have this understanding, the law written in their hearts and the conviction of the Spirit, and the wonder of creation and even the example of mercy towards the saved believer...and still don't repent towards the gospel, perishing in their sins.

But these people being described know the truth of God and hold it in unrighteousness. They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. They reject the truth for a lie. They worship themselves and the created over the Creator. And God gives them up to a reprobate (rejected) mind.
