For those that not only had the manifest truth of God, but a clear articulation of the gospel of grace and reconciliation through faith in Christ Jesus, understand it, and even profess to assent to it, and then reject it? They are worse off than those that simply never hear or consider it.
These have forsaken the right way;

**2 Peter 2:17**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.*

The apostates are reprobate, twice-dead. Not only dead and hellbound in the next world, but conscience seared and accursed in this one.
**2 Peter 2:21**
*For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.*

But we who have trusted the truth in our hearts have a more sure hope. We have the Spirit of truth to defend us from the spirit of error. Jesus said it is impossible to fool the elect.

But for the fallen away, God gives them strong delusions as punishment for their rejection of the truth.

2 **Thessalonians 2:10–12**
*And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness*.

But praise God this is not possible for a believer. We are kept from falling by the power of God. By the witness of the Spirit. By the perfect work of Christ, knowing we have not believed in vain.

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

Regarding the lie that those who are saved CAN fall away, can believe a strong delusion, can be fooled, the Bible teaches this is not possible.

**1 John 2:18–27**
*Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time. **They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us**. **But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things. I have not written unto you because ye know not the truth, but because ye know it,** and that no lie is of the truth.

Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son. Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also.

Let that therefore abide in you, which ye have heard from the beginning. **If that which ye have heard from the beginning shall remain in you, ye also shall continue in the Son, and in the Father**. And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life. These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you. **But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie**, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.*

John continues;

**1 John 4:1–6**
*Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. **Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.** They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and **the world heareth them**. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** **Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.***

This is the unction of the holy Spirit. This Spirit of truth. That we hear those of God and reject those heard of the world by their false teaching.

**John 10:1–5**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out. And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice. *

***And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.***

We who are saved WILL NOT FOLLOW the stranger. We hear Jesus' voice. This is the promise of God.

**John 10:26–30**
*But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand. I and my Father are one.*

It is impossible for a saved child of God to fall away into apostasy. The trust in a false way, after knowing and assenting to the truth in their hearts. And it is impossible for an apostate to ever be saved once they've rejected the truth.

**Hebrews 6:4–6**
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

Anyone teaching that saved believers can reject the truth, believe a lie, have strong delusion, and apostasize, is wrong. It's heresy. It is not possible.

Just as it is not possible for one who went out from us, who held the truth in unrighteousness and didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge, to ever come to the knowledge of the truth.

The Bible warns repeatedly against false prophets, false teachers who try to lead away people with itching ears by their vain jangling. Creeping unawares in order to spy out our liberty, and to make merchandise of us.

Just like Satan, they try to make you doubt God's word in order to get you to sin. Or to believe foolishness. A saved believer can be led away into believing some heresies that are couched in the truth.

These heresies are not necessarily apostasy. In order for it to be apostasy, it has to change the truth of God into a lie.

Not all heresies are damnable. Not all heresies force someone to become apostates by their adopting them as a school of thought or a systematic that they apply to or over their existing faith.

Nor does a heart that is no longer perfect towards God, but has added other elements of worship into their true faith, make someone an apostate. Yes they are not right and yes they are backslidden and yes they will face the chastening of God, but they have not lost their salvation. Theologians call adding falsehoods or heresies to true faith syncretism.

Solomon was guilty of this. He never rejected the Lord God or the temple he was given to build or the covenant and sacrifices that represented the Christ to come. But his heart was turned away to other gods by the love of his wives, partaking in their idolatry in addition to the truth he held in his heart.

This applies to saved believers who use terms like repent of your sins, or who believe in some of the elements of Calvinism and predestination. Or who get caught up in other false doctrines, or never fully abandon the religion that they were won out of.

It may apply to someone who trusted in Christ at the door when a soul winner came and presented the gospel to them, but out of habit and loyalty and family ties they continue on going to a Catholic Church for example.

Naaman was a Syrian general who asked the Lord for forgiveness for entering an idol's temple with his king, after believing on the truth of God.

**2 Kings 5:18**
*In this thing the LORD pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the LORD pardon thy servant in this thing.*

He had full knowledge of what he was doing and understood that it was wrong. I would assume Solomon did too, knowing the punishment he received through his son and the divided Kingdom for his spiritual adultery.

But there are thousands and thousands of saved believers who after trusting in God, and the blood of Christ, neglect to walk in the Spirit, and read the Bible and learn God's ways. Those who simply went back to their Catholic church or their Mormon church or whatever apostate cult they were in, and while it may prick them in the heart they might not recognize why.

But what they'll never do is trust in the false gospel of that church. Just as Naaman never trusted in the false gods of his people ever again.

And I think it's curious that this current heresy - that a saved believer could apostasize and could believe a false gospel in their heart, or reject the truth of God utterly, has been creeping up over the past few years.

It's a twist on Arianism, which holds that a saved believer can become apostate and lose salvation. By adding the assurance of salvation to it, it allows them to lead away babes in Christ or people who aren't fully trusting the truth, and give them cover to chase after delusions.

A believer they lead away with this vein jangling won't lose their salvation obviously. They also won't come to believe a lie ultimately because they can't. But they'll introduce doubt and they'll give a bad testimony and when the false teacher can get baby Christians to slander men of God, soul-winning efforts, the teaching of Truth, they ultimately hurt the cause of Christ.

But a nominal Christian, someone who has not fully believed unto salvation, it allows them to continue in whatever lie they are holding on to to avoid repentance.

And it softens them up to be led away by whatever other strange doctrine the false teacher decides to impart upon their proselytes. He makes them twofold more the child of Hell than themselves.

These false teachers are attempting to have it both ways. They use the comforting banner of "Once Saved, Always Saved" as a Trojan horse to smuggle in a license for total apostasy, claiming a person can completely deny Christ, turn to paganism, or become an atheist, and that God will simply override their will and force them to believe in the end.

This teaching collapses under the weight of Scripture for several critical reasons.

It redefines Faith as a meaningless past transaction, that purchased salvation, Rather than treating belief as a state of being. It becomes a transient action in their minds, rather than the reality their heart would live in if they believe the truth.

Of course we reject Calvinism, so there is no forcing of faith or salvation onto someone who has utterly rejected it. The Bible says they're ever learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Jesus says depart for me I never knew you.

It invents a class of people that the Bible doesn't say exists. There is a binary of those who believe and those who are condemned already because they have not believed. There is no third option.

They purposefully overlook the power of the Holy Spirit and His purpose, to seal the believer, guide us to all truth and show the spirit of error.

While that doesn't rise to the level of blaspheming the Holy Spirit, in my opinion, it sure does come close.

teachings.title: Belief as a state of being
teachings.summary: Argues that believe is a stative verb, so one cannot stop believing the truth without repenting of it, and quotes 2 Peter 3 on the unlearned wresting scripture.
teachings.text:
"Believe" is often misunderstood as an action, but it's generally a state of being. Like other "be" verbs (is, am, are), it reflects an internal condition—holding something as true in your mind.

For example, "I believe in kindness" describes a mental stance, not an act you perform. While it can seem active in some contexts, at its core, believing is a state of conviction. A state of being.

"Believe" and "be" verbs (like is, am, are, was, were) are typically classified as stative verbs when describing a state of being. Stative verbs express a condition, state, or situation that exists, rather than an action.

They express things like mental states, emotions, senses, possession, or existence, and typically don’t involve physical activity or change. Unlike action (or dynamic) verbs, which show something happening (e.g., "run," "write"), stative verbs indicate a steady, ongoing state.

Stative verbs are rarely used in continuous (progressive) tenses like "am believing" because states are seen as enduring, not temporary actions. Saying "I am knowing" sounds unnatural and stupid compared to "I know."

Understanding stative verbs helps in using correct grammar, especially avoiding progressive forms with verbs that don’t typically take them. It also clarifies why "believe"is generally a state of being—an internal condition—rather than an action.

Repentance, understood as a change of mind, is the pivotal means of transforming belief because it involves a deliberate shift in one’s perspective or conviction. Belief, as a stative verb, represents an enduring mental state, a settled acceptance of something as true. Without repentance—actively rethinking or rejecting a prior belief—this state persists, as beliefs tend to remain fixed unless consciously challenged. By engaging in repentance, one reorients their mind, replacing old convictions with new ones, thus enabling a fundamental change in belief.

This is why when someone says "I stopped believing Jesus was real and that God gave His Son," or "I stopped believing the gospel was by faith alone and joined the Catholic Church," what they are saying is the repented of the truth, the big capital-T Truth, to believe a lie.

The Bible says this is not possible. We have the Spirit of truth, cannot be deceived (it's not possible), and cannot reject it. But even if it were possible, it is IMPOSSIBLE for someone to be brought again to repentance. That's what **Hebrews 6** says and I believe it.

I figure if a mountain of scripture isn't sufficient for some people, a brief English lesson might be.

...*even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are **unlearned and unstable wrest**, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.*

teachings.title: The disciples' doubts were not apostasy
teachings.summary: Shows from John 6, Luke 24 and John 20:9 that the disciples believed yet did not grasp the resurrection, and that doubt differs from repenting of saving faith.
teachings.text:
The Gospels repeatedly show the disciples failing to grasp the necessity of Jesus' death and resurrection, even though they believed in Him for eternal salvation.

**John 6:68-69**
*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.
*
Their faith in Jesus as the Messiah and Savior was genuine, but their understanding of the Scriptures regarding His suffering, death, and resurrection was incomplete until after the resurrection, when He "opened up the scriptures to them" as described in **Luke 24:45-46**.

Jesus first explicitly foretold His death and resurrection after Peter's confession of faith (**Matthew 16:16; Mark 8:29; Luke 9:20**). The disciples' reaction shows they did not comprehend or accept it;

**Matthew 16:21-23**
*From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee. But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.

*Jesus explained to them, but they did not understand it. Peter's confession that Jesus was the Christ, shown to him by the Father according to Christ, the rock on which Jesus builds His church, was sufficient to save the apostle. Yet moments later Jesus calls him "Satan" rebuking Peter's offense at the idea of Jesus suffering death.

**Mark 8:31-33**
*And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him. But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.*

Was Peter in unbelief? No. He just didn't understand the concept of what would soon follow. He was saved by faith in the things he knew, under the Old Testament. Without the indwelling and seal of the Spirit, they did not fully comprehend the gospel of the New Testament.

**Luke 9:44-45**
*Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men. But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.*

As they approached Jerusalem, Jesus detailed His fate again, but the disciples could not fully understand.

**Luke 18:31-34**
*Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished. For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again. And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.

***John 12:16**
*These things understood not his disciples at the first: **but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him**, and that they had done these things unto him.

*It is a key point, raised again and again that they simply did not have it given them to understand.

**John 20:9**
*For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.*

And so, after the resurrection, you have scenes like the two pilgrims on the road to Emmaus (**Luke 24:13-32**). They didn't believe He had risen from the dead. They didn't know this was Jesus who spoke to them. Jesus says "*Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?"* and explains to them they should believe the prophets and expounded the Scriptures unto them, showing how His suffering and resurrection were foretold from Moses onward (**Genesis 3:15; Deuteronomy 18:15; Isaiah 53; Psalm 22:16-18; 16:10**).

They were believers, under the OT, who trusted that Jesus was the Christ but didn't understand the totality of what that meant, until it was given to them to understand.

The same with the apostles who didn't believe Mary Magdalene's report. Not that they stopped believing Jesus was Christ, or stopped believing the word of God they knew and understood unto salvation.

They just didn't believe a woman's story. Same as Thomas didn't believe them. He still knew Jesus was the Messiah, but he didn't trust their accounts that He had risen from the dead, because none of them really could understand that aspect without Jesus' instruction and the Spirit that then came and sealed them.

These passages demonstrate that the disciples' faith for salvation was present early, but full insight into the Scriptures' prophecies about the Messiah's suffering and resurrection required Jesus' post-resurrection teaching.

People, who err not knowing scripture, will often take a verse out of context, or use a word that doesn't mean what they think it does in the situation, and apply it in isolation as a proof text for heresy and nonsense.

We should search the scriptures to see if something is so. Rightly dividing the word of God. And ask more mature Christians if what you think something means, does, or has a larger context you might be missing.

And it shouldn't have to be said that the doubting Thomases among the disciples of Christ during that 3 days and 3 nights, never repented of their faith to believe on something else.

They never became apostates. They didn't say, "Well Jesus is dead, I'm going to become a Pharisee." Or "God doesn't even be real!"

Christians all have moments of doubt and lack of faith, but what they will never do is repent of that saving faith to believe a lie instead.

teachings.title: Believing is not a work, and the apostate
teachings.summary: Gathers Romans 4:5, Hebrews 3, Philippians 1:6, 1 John 5:4, Romans 10:13, John 15:6 and 2 Peter 2 to show salvation is not lost and that apostates were never saved.
teachings.text:
**Romans 4:5 **
*But to him that **worketh not**,** but believeth** on him that justifieth the ungodly, **his faith** is counted for righteousness.*

**Hebrews 3:12-14**
*Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end*

**Galatians 5:4**
*Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.*

It goes on and on and on and on...

**Philippians 1:3-6**
*I thank my God upon every remembrance of you, Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ*

**1 John 5:4**
*For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.*

If you believe that an apostate is able to come again unto repentance then your argument is with God.

**Romans 10:13**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved*.

**John 15:6**
*If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.*

You cannot lose your salvation once you've been born again. When you have trusted on Christ Jesus, believing the truth that you have eternal life as a free gift of the Father, you are quickened. Sealed by the Spirit. Held by the power of God.

So what does this verse mean?

**2 Peter 2:17-22**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. **But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.***

Wonder what this could possibly mean? **🤔**

teachings.title: Assurance and the perseverance promise
teachings.summary: Says believers can be assured they will never perish, and that enduring to the end in the Gospels is a promise for those living through the tribulation, not about spiritual salvation.
teachings.text:
"Believers in Christ can be personally assured that they WILL NEVER PERISH FOREVER because their salvation rests solely upon the faithfulness and finished work of the Savior on their behalf."

So true. **Believers** in Christ have that blessed assurance. People who believe in vain and depart from the faith never believed in the first place, and don't have that assurance.

"Perseverance of the saints" has nothing to do with spiritual salvation or anything else regarding the gospel. It's a promise made by Jesus to people who are alive during tribulation that if they endure to the end of that tribulation, they will be saved out of it by the coming of the Lord.

Heretics and fools twist the meaning to apply it to the gospel. They hate the word of God and have to take things wildly out of context to try and make their foolish and unbiblical arguments.

teachings.title: Confessing faults and repenting as a believer
teachings.summary: Teaches that saved believers should admit their sin to God and stop it, and confess faults to one another according to James 5:16.
teachings.text:
There is a repentance of sin that all saved believers should strive to do, admitting your faults and iniquities to God, and then turning from those things. To be honest with yourself and God.

He doesn't want you to be sorry, or need you to be sorrowful, the Lord just wants you to admit it's wrong and stop it.

So do most normal, healthy people. Parents understand. People who have had relationships with family or friends with drug addiction or other similar behaviors, they understand. No one wants to hear excuses. No one wants a slobbering apology. Just admit you were wrong, to God at least, and stop doing whatever it was. Especially be willing to make amends with the brethren;

**James 5:16**
*Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.*

You want your fervent prayer to avail much? Confess your faults and pray for each other. And forgive your brother when he does, as you would be forgiven.

teachings.title: The parable of the sower
teachings.summary: Notes that in Matthew 13 the wayside hearers are unsaved while the other three receive the word, though only the last bring forth fruit.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 13:18-23 **
*Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower. When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.

But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is **he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it**; Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.

He also that **received seed** among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and **he becometh unfruitful**.

But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; **which also beareth fruit, **and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.*

Note that in the parable of the sower, the first group are unsaved, those of the wayside.

The other 3 are saved, receiving the word, but for the reasons given, the 2nd and 3rd aren't fruitful or become unfruitful. Yet they still are saved. The 4th are successful Christians, fruitful in bringing forth more believers, winning souls.

There is no example of someone who receives the seed, then becomes the hardpan ground of the wayside, no longer believing, and then sprouting and growing roots yet again

teachings.title: Paul kept the faith
teachings.summary: Reads 2 Timothy 4 to show that Paul's 'kept the faith' refers to his ministry and reward, not holding on to personal belief to stay saved.
teachings.text:
2 Timothy 4:1-13
 *I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom; Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine. For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables. But watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry. For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.*

Paul, in an emotionally charged farewell to Timothy, and really to the reader, says he is ready to die. He has run the race set before him, as He says in **Hebrews 12:1-3**
*Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
*
In the King James, a keeper is a person or entity that holds, guards, maintains, or has custody of something or someone. This can refer to someone like a prison keeper, the keeper of a park or flock, or someone responsible for a sacred place. The concept extends to holding a position of oversight, like a keeper of the great seal, or having a moral responsibility for another's welfare, as seen in the question "Am I my brother's keeper?"

Paul is talking about his life of ministry, as a keeper of the faith, as the evangelist to the Gentiles. Paul kept the faith and would expect a crown of righteousness for his reward, for those works.

This has nothing to do with holding on to personal beliefs.

Context matters.

teachings.title: Against continual believism
teachings.summary: Answers the teaching that belief must be maintained until death, using John 3, Galatians 4, 1 Corinthians 15 and Hebrews 6 to show that vain faith means never having believed.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth** in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth** on him is not condemned: but **he that believeth not** is condemned already, **because he hath not believed** in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

Calvinism falsely teaches that election is unconditional, that grace is irresistible and that belief is conferred on people by force of God's sovereign will. That they are chosen to have faith thrust upon them. (Some Calvinists will say at that point, there's a choice, but generally, they reject free will).

Saved Christians understand that there is one condition for salvation, and that condition is to believe on Christ. To believe in the name of the only begotten Son. He that believes that the Father so loved the world He gave His Son, Who while we were yet sinners, died for us, and rose again that we may have eternal life in His name.

This is Biblical repentance. **Acts 19:3-5** defines it for us.

*And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with **the baptism of repentance**, saying unto the people, **that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.** When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.*

Repentance towards the truth, the Gospel of God, is to believe on Christ Jesus. And believe means to trust.

Ephesians 1:12-14
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, **who first trusted in Christ**. In whom **ye also trusted**, **after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation:** in whom also **after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise**, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Repent>believe>trust is all one thing, the Bible says. This is the condition by which one is saved.

"But what if I stop believing?" What if you stopped trusting that the Gospel is true? What if you repent again to something else? How? There is no biblical mechanism given where this happens, where a saved believer stops believing.

There are examples given for those who backslide, who lose the joy of their salvation, who walk in the flesh, who are carnal Christians, who don't feed the Spirit, and become castaways to the calling of God. Chastened, prodigal, all of these things are given us as examples for what may happen in the Christian life of saved believers.

But there is only one doctrine given for those that claimed to have believed and then repented to believe, to trust on something else. That they never fully believed. That they believed in vain. That it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance.

Paul, upon hearing the church at Galatia had those among its members who were being beguiled into adopting the law to be saved, who had repented of the faith he taught them to believe something else - he wrote to them and harshly questioned if they actually were saved.

**Galatians 3:1-7**
*O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, **that ye should not obey the truth,** before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you? **This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?** Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? Have ye suffered so many things **in vain?** if it be yet in vain. He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.*

Note that Paul doesn't say "Well you did believe, so you're still saved," and then try and get them to change their mind again. He accuses them of not believing at all.

**Galatians 4:4-11, 14-20**
*But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods. But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.*..*Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them. But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.
*
According to this new group of people claiming "Heresy!" Paul was a heretic to be marked and avoided.

Also John then, according to these foolish men, would be a heretic, for teaching that if one goes out from the doctrine of the truth, it was to make manifest that they never believed.

**1 Corinthians 15:12-14**
*Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.*

Faith in vain is defined for us again here, where those that had heard the truth preached, that included the resurrection of the dead, now were saying the resurrection of Christ wasn't true. Paul says that this means their faith was in vain. Empty. Having no effect. Vanity is defined again and again in scripture to mean one thing, a belief or action that has no power towards salvation in God. Vain works, vain idols, vain beliefs. *All is vanity, sayeth the preacher*, but one truth: *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man*, and so we are called to *Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth*. To believe. To trust. To keep in remembrance. To turn away from vanity.

Finally, this strange doctrine being promoted by very foolish men says that it is not only **possible** that *those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance*, but that God actually will force repentance and impose faith again upon the apostate, before they die, so that they are kept saved by God's sovereign will.

A form of Ultra-Calvinism.

They claim, contrary to God's word, that those that *crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame*, those who go out from us and are manifest that they were not of us, will, by the sovereignty of God, be brought to faith, "believing again" just in time to not perish.

Despite the fact that the Bible says this is impossible. Despite the fact that they claim to reject Calvinism.

They so badly want to have the ability to reject God, kill the new man, break the seal of the Spirit, and still be "saved," they've invented a foolish and damnable heresy that tells people who reject the truth to not worry about it. They "believed" once, and that's good enough and if they trust in something else later, oh well.

Paul wrote entire Epistles in the Spirit to warn against believing in vain. Telling people to keep in memory the truth of the Gospel he preached.

Because once you believe the truth, once you repent, once you trusted on Christ Jesus alone to be saved, you have the Spirit of truth, and not the spirit of error, and cannot be deceived.

**1 John 4:2-6**
*Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.*

There is a heresy that is called "Continual Believeism" that teaches, among other damnable heresies (repent-of-your-sin, baptism for babies, etc) that "belief" is a work, an action. That "belief" isn't simply knowing something is true but requires ongoing, active faith maintained until death. A "perseverance of the saints," that makes a state of mind into a process. Just as they make repentance into a process.

The new, foolish application of this heresy makes the same mistake those who actually endorse "Continual Believeism." They too make what is a change of mind and a knowledge that something is true into a process and a work.

They make the same damned error.

The ""Continual Believeism" heretics say that believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe or through unrepentant sin.

The people taking that heresy and twisting it to mean that "believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe," but they will be forced to believe again, because they "had been saved."

It's two heads of the same damned coin and a misunderstanding of what believing is, simply repenting to the knowledge something is true, accepting something true as true, trusting on it being true.

They turn it into an action, a work, and wrest with scripture to deal with it, rather than accepting that all those who have believed for salvation just know that what they trusted in is true, even if they doubt themselves, because it is the promise of God.

Call me Colombo, because one more thing; these fools are also applying the same logic Dispensationalists hold regarding the Jews.

That a promise of God is a promise, and so that even though the Jews are unrepentant antichrists who rejected Jesus, they will somehow still be saved in the end because they had a covenant. That in the end, God will give them faith and they will believe, and so "all Israel shall be saved!"

The covenant with physical Israel was conditional. They no longer have the promises because they broke the condition. They held the truth in unrighteousness, and did not wish to retain God in their knowledge.

Salvation is conditional on belief, on knowing in our hearts that Jesus is the Christ. *If thou believest with all thine heart*...If you don't know that something is true with all your heart, you don't believe it. If you know something is true with all your heart, how could you ever reject it?

It doesn't mean you have to continually work to believe. It doesn't mean you have to constantly remind yourself that it's true that the only way a man may be saved is by faith alone in the finished work of Christ.

It just is.

If you come up with a doctrine that contradicts clear scripture, it falls on you to explain it and make it consistent.

If you cannot explain Hebrews 6 and 1 John 2, to make it fit your opinion, then your opinion is wrong.

teachings.title: Believed in vain

teachings.title: Entering the rest in Hebrews
teachings.summary: Shows from Hebrews 4 that only those who believed the promise entered Christ's rest, and that sin does not lose salvation while those who reject the truth for their own works were never saved.
teachings.text:
*Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you **should seem to come short of it.** For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached **did not profit them, not being mixed with faith** in them that heard it. For we which **have believed** do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world. For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works. And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest. Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and **they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:** Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts. **For if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day**. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. **For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his**. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest**, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.***
...
***Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.** But exhort one another daily, while it called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. **For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;** While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, **harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.** For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? **And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? **Hebrews** teaches clearly that only those who have believed the promise, and entered into the rest of Christ Jesus, are saved.

It does not say if we sin, we lose salvation. It doesn't say if we forget our rest, we aren't saved. Paul writes that those without faith unto salvation, who heard the word and yet turned to their own works, and hardened their hearts, never entered into that rest.

teachings.title: Struggling faith versus rejecting the truth

If a person’s faith falters, fails, or is unfruitful will that person be lost? No. Of course not.

**2 Peter 2:21-22**
*For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. Dogs. Swine. Reprobates. Falling away and believing in vain.

teachings.title: The prodigal son and biblical repentance
teachings.summary: Reads Luke 15 as a picture of the Father's love for His children and of repentance as turning toward Him, not sorrow, willingness to work, or making Him lord.
teachings.text:
**Luke 15:11-24**
*And he said, A certain man had two sons: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: and bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.*

In this beautiful picture of the Father's love for His children, which teaches God's unconditional love for those that are His, even when we backslide, even when we despise our inheritance and go after the world in sin. Even as we served other masters and feed the swine. That no matter what, we may return to the Father.

More, we see that even though it may be important for us to feel the need to be full of sorrow and remorse at having gone astray, and to want to work it off, to be worthy of the Father, God isn't interested in any of that. Only that you turn towards Him.

We see the father runs to meet the son. He ignores the son's groveling. Even before the son gets it out the Father has hugged and kissed him. He doesn't even get a chance to offer to work off his sins, the Father sends for him to be clothed in the best robes, given a ring and shoes. To be made whole in the gift of the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. And a joyous feast is called to celebrate.

Blessed is the man to whom God will not impute sin. Blessed are we who have been forgiven.

When the son *came to himself*, is the moment of repentance. That he needed salvation from the state he was in. Being hungry and without, led him to it.

It was that turning towards the Father that shows repentance. Not his sorrow and regret. Not his willingness to work, or wanting to make his father his lord.

It was his coming towards the father, who seeing him afar off ran to meet him.

That is biblical repentance. It's all God asks of us. That we turn to Him and allow Him to clothe us in righteousness that we did not earn or expect or deserve. And to rejoice, celebrating our reconciliation.

teachings.title: Metanoia: repentance is a change of mind toward God
teachings.summary: Explains the word translated repentance as a change of mind and heart toward God and belief, and argues that adding "of sin" came with modern versions.
teachings.text:
*Metanoia*, the Greek word translated in our King James Bible as "repentance," is a changing of the mind. “Meta” comes from the root for “after” or “beyond,” while “noeo” is “to think.” So metanoeo means to reconsider or to rethink something. At its root, repentance is about changing one's mind. 'Metanoia' literally means to 'change your mind, to change direction' …has nothing to do with guilt or shame.

So, when John the Baptist calls his audience to repent, he is telling them to understand the Kingdom is at hand and to have a thorough change of heart and mind regarding salvation and the coming Christ. To reconsider and believe. To be convicted in the Spirit. To turn towards God.

This has always been its meaning and no one changed it until modern Bible versions in the 20th century began to append "..of sin" and delete the instances of God's repentance, to begin pushing the Devil's favorite damnable heresy, works salvation.

That's why in scripture, again and again, repentance and belief are used in tandem to express conversion, by believing on Jesus and receiving the gift of eternal life promised by God.

This is the Gospel of the Bible and how men have been saved from the time of Seth. The notion that it was changed or twisted in the 1980s to something other than that is not only biblically and linguistically wrong, it is absurd.

" In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Feel bad about sinning and try not to sin: for the kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

Hey that sounds like works...

*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.*

Would Jesus be telling the Jews of the gospel of grace by say to them "**Behave**, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand," *or* "**Believe**, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand?"

Which way of saying it fits the gospel?

Would He be telling Jews to clean up their acts, or to believe they need salvation, and that that salvation, promised by God, was at hand?

teachings.title: Repentance and the gospel: not "of your sins"
teachings.summary: Argues that adding "of your sins" to repent changes the gospel, and that biblical repentance is a change of heart toward believing God for salvation by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
Generally when the doctrine of repentance comes up, we think of false prophets like Ray Comfort, or John Macarthur, Lordshippers and others who add the teaching of works to justification by faith.

These vipers are neo-Catholics who deny the glory of God revealed in our redemption, found only in His grace and by the blood of Christ, eternal life in His resurrection, reconciliation and forgiveness, adoption into the kingdom. Heirs to the promise.

They add works of the law to justification and keep people in perpetual doubt of if they are truly saved. It is a means of control and it denies the liberty found in the Lord Jesus.

There are others, many well meaning believers, who have been raised with false Bible versions, or taught by honest pastors misled by Bible college or extrabiblical reading, into appending "...of your sins" to the word repent.

This phrase never appears in scripture.

And, in my experience, these people are straining at a rhetorical gnat and swallowing a camel, by trying to square their trust in salvation by grace through faith, with a vain tradition. They create a semantic trap for themselves, to the detriment of the Gospel.

They will say that repent of sins actually just means acknowledging you're a sinner **which is** part of biblical repentance. If we can't acknowledge we're sinners in need of salvation, how in the world could we accept the free gift of it?

And God's not going to quibble with them over their misunderstanding of the term or use of it.

Brothers shouldn't fight each other over pedantic semantics.

However, the danger of being trapped in that snare of allowing the preaching of men to autocomplete a biblical phrase with something that doesn't appear in the text, comes when you're giving people the gospel. It's sows confusion, and here is how.

Let's just say someone approaches you online or in real life and says that they are heartbroken. They feel worthless and trapped in sin. They have an addiction or are in a position where they can't break free. They know they are damned, know God is real and have a head knowledge that Jesus might be the answer they are seeking, because the Spirit is working in them.

And they desperately need help.

And one comes to them and says, that all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God, there are none righteous. That we're all sinners, deserving death and hell, the good news is Jesus paid that price for us and we only have to believe on Him and be saved. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. That we may have peace with God through His son, with the eternal security that, even though we may sin in the flesh, we are sealed by the Spirit unto the day of redemption.

(This obviously is an abridged version of the Roman's road, where we show them from scripture all of these points because faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God, I am summarizing because I am writing to those who have accepted this all to be true and called upon the name of the Lord, Jesus Christ, that they may be healed.)

And say another says to them repent of your sins and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and thou shall be saved.

The first example is using scripture that is very specific of what you need to believe, to repent towards, that they may be saved. It is good news. They feel trapped and unworthy. They are told that, just as they are God will forgive them in Christ. That none are worthy but God so loved us that He gave His only begotten Son. Leading them to say "Lord, have mercy on me, a sinner," and believe that in Jesus name they are forgiven.

Jesus said our mission statement as Christians is to preach this good news to every creature.

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised*.

The second, even if they are well meaning and have the best of intentions to win these people to Christ, actually create more of a problem, because to the unsaved they only hear the first part and see it as the very obstacle they already told you they are struggling with.

"I have to repent of my sins? What does that mean? Turn from my sins? Which ones? All of them? What if I can't? What if I relapse? What about things I didn't know were sins? Does it just mean willing to give up sin? I wish I could!"

It is bad news. We need Jesus because we are broken. Even the unregenerate man regrets their sin and dreads the looming punishment for it. How does telling them to turn from the sin they are trapped in in order to believe and be saved, save anyone?

And even if you're saved by faith, if you give this as your gospel, You're going to have people who could have been saved, who desperately needed to hear the truth, discouraged and turned away.

They may as well have gone to Ray Comfort for the gospel. Gene Kim. Some other reprobate. The Catholic Church.

We don't get healed that we can come to Christ. We come to Christ so that we may be healed.

*Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved*.

I've done it before in past channels and it may have migrated its way to here, but I have literally gone over every single appearance of repentance in the Bible or any deviation thereof, and shown systematically what is being repented from and towards in each case.

This isn't some new doctrine found only in YouTube. This isn't some apostasy that came about in the last century.

This is the gospel of God as it's taught in the Bible.

While there may be secondary or tertiary doctrines that you don't like about certain preachers or pastors or soul winners or evangelists or any other saved Christian under the sun who's been saved by grace through faith, or if you've had personality conflicts or past experiences that traumatized you or any other thing other than biblical truth that leads you to doubt that repentance is a change of heart towards believing God that one might be saved in Christ, pray on it. That God may remove the thorns from your heart, so that you may be in better service to Hm and giving the gospel to others.

Stop slandering people who have successfully and consistently given the gospel and gotten thousands of people saved.

teachings.title: Can a Christian Take the Mark of the Beast?
teachings.summary: Answers an interview claiming saved Christians could take the mark or be punished in the Millennium, showing from Matthew 24, Revelation 3, 13 and 14 and 1 Thessalonians 5 that the saved are sealed and cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
In comments, someone posted a video by Kent Hovind, a disgraced former pastor who has some clout still in truther circles for his defense of biblical creation vs evolution. Though much of the rest of his doctrine is a mess., His personal life has left him unqualified to be a pastor, and demonstrated questionable character, but the debates he engages in with atheists over evolution draw in new followers all the time.

In this video that someone posted, Hovind gives time to a wicked heretic that I won't bother to name, who came to prominence in some evangelical circles nearly a decade ago, promoting a book based on the unbiblical idea that saved Christians could go to Hell during the Millennial Reign.

Often mocked as "Baptist purgatory doctrine," its promotion exposed many popular very-online pastors as false prophets.

Hovind begins by saying he "wonders what will happen if a Christian takes the mark" and starts the interview by saying to the viper who authored this heresy "I didn't want to believe it, but having read your book I can't say that it's wrong."

But the Bible can, and does.

In **Matthew 24:24** says of the end times;

*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. *

It's not possible because the saved have the seal of the Holy Spirit upon us, and He lives within us.

The Bible says in Revelation chapter 13 that the false prophet, who will perform great wonders and deceive many to worship the beast and take the mark; *and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed. And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads:And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.*

Further, in chapter 14, the Bible says;

*And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand, The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.*

While in chapter 3 of Revelation, Christ promises the saved "*shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.*"

Those who are saved, whose names are in the book of life CANNOT take the mark. Again, chapter 13;* all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life.*

But further, irrespective of the mark, could backslidden Christians not be taken in rapture after the tribulation, and be present both for God's wrath and punished with Hell for a thousand years? Again, no.

**1 Thessalonians 5:9**
*For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ.*

We are saved by faith alone, not of works. If someone has believed, the Bible says, they shall not come into condemnation but have eternal life. This is the good news. This is the Gospel.

This twisted damnable heresy hinges on the behavior of Christians, their works, to save them from Hell, even if it is for "only" the thousand years of the Millennial Reign. It's wicked as Hell, as the viper who promoted it and all the false teachers who gave it an airing will find out.

teachings.title: Does everyone sin?
teachings.summary: Answers from Romans 3:23 and 1 John 2:2 that all have sinned and need Christ as the sole propitiation, and that believers have eternal life that cannot be lost because they are sealed by the Holy Spirit. Quotes 1 John 1:9-10 and 2:1.
teachings.text:
"Does everyone sin?"

The Bible says *for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God,* and so we need to be saved. We need Christ to be the sacrifice, the sole propitiation for our sin. *And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.* Past. Present. Future. We are forgiven in Christ. The Bible says if we believe, *We **have** eternal life. *Everlasting. That can never be lost or taken away, because by the holy Spirit of God we are *sealed unto the day of redemption.*

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.*

Amen

teachings.title: Do you believe the record?
teachings.summary: Quotes 1 John 5:10-14 and asks whether the reader believes God's record that eternal life is a gift in His Son alone. Says that to think it can be lost or earned is to call God a liar.
teachings.text:
**1 John 5**

*10 He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.
*
11 *And this is the record, that* **God** **hath** **given** **to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son**.

*12 He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

13 These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.

14 And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:*

Do you believe that record? That salvation is a gift, given by God or eternal life, everlasting, never to die or see Hell, in Jesus, alone. Can't be lost. Can't be earned by other means. Paid for by Christ.

If you think it can be lost, or must be achieved or maintained by your own works, or that it's not knowable, that you can't have confidence in this gift, then you're calling God a liar.

teachings.title: Saved Christians forget they were sinners
teachings.summary: Observes that many Christians act as though they were never sinners or backslidden after salvation. Says most believers go through backsliding and that real maturity admits sin and shows grace to others.
teachings.text:
I think a lot of Christians, especially online (but even before there was an internet believe me), but a lot of Christians act as though they were never sinners or backslidden after they've been saved. The average span of zealous devotion in the faith is something like 3 years. It generally takes the old man about 3 years to push his way back after one receives the new man.

Some people remain cast away for the rest of their natural life, even though they have that eternal reward waiting. Many eventually mature and come to understand the awesomeness of the gift they've been given. But most go through some form of backsliding, or falling away.

The cares of the world come for us all in different ways through different means, and the devil is like a ravenous lion seeking whom he can devour.

But, most Christians will portray themselves as having always been perfect in their ways. They may admit to a sinful past as part of a testimony to how much they've changed, but it's rare they'll admit their own sins. It takes a kind of maturity in Christ and in faith to be able to.

I mean, when you ask them they'll all admit of course I'm a sinner, but few really mean it because we all want to look good. But you can tell when someone has had a sincere repentance from whatever had taken them away from their love of the Gospel.

teachings.title: Once saved always saved: proof texts
teachings.summary: A run of passages for the security of the believer: kept by the power of God in 1 Peter 1, Galatians 5 against adding a work, Hebrews 13:5 and Deuteronomy 31:6 on never being forsaken, and 1 John 5 on eternal life given in the Son.
teachings.text:
**1 Peter 1:4-9**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath **begotten us again** **unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,** **To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,
Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.** Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:
That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:
Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:
Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.*

Anyone who says we are not saved unto everlasting life, with eternal security, is a liar and is damned. If you're caught up in this false teaching, repent and believe the word of God.

**Galatians 5**
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.

2 Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.

3 For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

4 Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.

5 For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith.

6 For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.*

If you are counting on your own ability not to sin, you are a debtor to the whole of the law and Christ is of no effect. You are fallen from grace. Not in the sense that you've lost your salvation, but that you've never had it.

You can substitute anything in the place of circumcision in this chapter. Baptism, repenting of sin, going to church... anything, and once you add any condition to the grace and faith in Christ to your belief for salvation (or maintaining salvation) you now are a debtor to the WHOLE of the Law. "*If you offend in one point," *in commission or omission, you are damned. *Christ is become of no effect unto you.*

"Repent of sins" or "you can lose your salvation" are damnable heresy because no one can repent of all sin, and no one saved by faith alone can lose it. Anyone giving these as part of their "gospel" is a false teacher who isn't giving people a "lively hope," but an impossible task.

Literally there were people at the church of Galatia convinced that they needed to do *something *in order to be saved. They added a work to the Gospel, and Paul head to write to tell them that in doing so they made the Gospel of no effect. The same impulse rules men today that make them unable to believe that God would give them eternal life with no strings attached, and the delusion they place themselves under to maintain that false belief keeps them fallen from grace.

Ok, one more swing at this dead horse:

**Hebrews 13:5** 
*Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.*

**Deuteronomy 31:6**
*Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.*

How can you be content with what you have, be strong and without fear, if you believe God the Father will abandon you? How can you call Him a liar when He says He will never leave or forsake His children?

I think one of the most toxic things about the current culture of illegitimacy and divorce we are mired in, that all of us have experienced either directly, as children or in our families, makes people suspicious of unconditional love, and unable to grasp a heavenly Father who won't abandon His sons

Ok, one more proof text for OSAS. Don't miss it, or you might be calling God who cannot lie a liar:


**1 John 5**
*7 For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.

8 And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one.

9 If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.

10 He that believeth on the Son of God **hath the witness in himself**: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.

11 And this is the record, that God hath given to us **eternal** life, and this life is in his Son*

teachings.title: Counted as sheep for the slaughter, yet faithful
teachings.summary: Psalm 44 shows the faithful, who cannot apostatize, can suffer without being punished for sin, and Paul uses it to show God eventually delivers His people.
teachings.text:
What makes **Psalm 44** so jarring and often makes modern readers uncomfortable, is that the congregation is stating they are not being punished for apostasy or adultery or for being unfaithful.

In many other laments, Israel confesses their sins and acknowledges that their defeat is a righteous judgment from God. But here, they boldly declare their innocence:

*All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant... If we have forgotten the name of our God... Shall not God search this out?*

Travails come upon the just. Upon the faithful who have placed their trust in the Lord.

The psalmists raise a relevant point today; believers may cry out to God and ask why they are suffering, knowing they have not fallen to apostasy.

These sons of Korah are believers, and believers cannot apostatize. They feel confident in asking God to search their hearts for any sign of adultery in worship of Him.

They may, amongst themselves, talk about how the northern kingdom of Israel which was also being afflicted in this time by the Assyrian empire, deserved it. They had fallen into the sin of Jeroboam and gone after strange gods.

But these faithful Levites could wonder what they themselves may have done to bring upon these attacks.

Whatever other sins they may have had in their lives or collectively, they still were faithful to the Lord.

They did exactly what Deuteronomy 6 commanded. They listened to their fathers. They trusted not in their own bows or swords. They kept the faith, yet they were still *scattered among the heathen* and *counted as sheep for the slaughter*, and yet still faced tribulation.

Paul quotes **Psalm 44** in **Romans** for exactly this reason. To show that God eventually does deliver the faithful. That we can count on him even when it seems like the entire world is against us.

Paul is using the same technique of teaching to the children the stories of the fathers, to bring us hope. Judah was delivered from the Assyrians. And the faithful were delivered by the promise of Christ being fulfilled.

Using then a past lament to give future hope, and show the strength of God in keeping His promises is the entire point of the commandment.

We see the Deliverance of God's people into the promised land in the past used as hope for the people then present Jerusalem, and their cries are then given to us as hope today knowing that they were eventually delivered.

If we are scattered to the wilderness, to the place of dragons, or are led through the valley of the shadow of death, we have that hope within us. The call to have the patience of Job. The faith of the fathers. The understanding of Paul.

So stand fast and comfort one another with these words.

teachings.title: Begin with confession: a warning to prayer warriors
teachings.summary: Effective prayer reminds God of His promises and begins with honest confession, guarding prayer warriors against creeping pride.
teachings.text:
David establishes this truth early in the psalm for a reason, which is made clear as it goes along.

It isn't so much as David brags about his charitable heart to the poor, but in the opening verses, he humbly reminds himself and the Lord he is petitioning of the promises He has made.

Then, the prayer moves to confession. The honest assessment of the heart before a holy, holy, holy God.

This pattern of reminders and confession, before petition, is helpful to keep in mind for our prayer life, if we want it to be successful.

We often hear about "prayer warriors," those who are continuously in prayer, especially for others. Who seek the burdens of others to bring them before the Lord, and it is a wonderful work.

But as we seek to be counted among the elite forces of prayer, we should always keep in mind the humility and confession that makes our prayer life effective.

And so when David writes *be merciful unto me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee*, we need to take it to heart in our own approach to the Throne. The man who was the apple of God's eye was honest in his confession. The King of Israel was lowly enough to be convicted as he approached the Throne of Grace.

Watch out for the creeping pride that may come from being recognized as a "prayer warrior," and the audacity that may infect what is a great habit. The loss of the love of others that should drive it, but iniquity creeping in.

Begin with confession. A contrite heart with love unfeigned can move mountains.

teachings.title: Many are the afflictions of the righteous
teachings.summary: God's commandments are for our good and He provides for His own, yet the godly will suffer affliction that grows faith, and none who trust Him will be desolate.
teachings.text:
Those that trust in the Lord know they shall never want. We are protected from evil by a host of angels. We are given our daily bread.

**Psalms 37:25**
*I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread*.

We may not be rich, we may not be feasting on expensive meals. But the Lord will provide for his own.

And the Lord promises us that we shall have a long life with good in it if we keep ourselves from speaking lies and doing evil, and rather seek peace and pursue it. Loving our neighbors.

While the Commandments of the Lord serve to let us know that we have fallen short of His perfect ways, they are given that it be well with us. That if we follow them, we have an easier life full of blessings. They are for our benefit, not to oppress us.

We are judged by the law of Liberty, not saved by our works. But our works can benefit us in our service to God.

God's eyes are upon us and he listens for our prayers, when we walk in the truth. And he is against those who commit evil, and he chastens every son He receives.

*Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.*

**2 Timothy 3:12**
*Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution*.

While we are promised a longer life with more blessings, we are not promised a carefree life that has no suffering. Often the suffering we experience is for our benefit to help us grow in the Lord, and to increase our faith.

Praise and obedience and calling upon the Lord, and the tribulations that we suffer, all work together for good. Because they increase our faith.

The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be desolate.

This is the promise given to all believers. That once we are saved we are always saved.b that we shall never be left desolate. Will never be ashamed for our trust in the Lord.

He will redeem The souls of his servants and bring us out of tribulation and into Glory, in His holy name. Amen

teachings.title: Length of days forever, and the fire that devours
teachings.summary: Those who call on the Lord are given eternal life forever, while the wicked who reject Him are swallowed up in His wrath and fire.
teachings.text:
